body_en: US president confirms Susie Wiles, current chief of staff and first woman to serve in the role, will step down

Stephen Miller, Donald Trump ’s most controversial aide and the architect of his sweeping immigration crackdown, will become his new White House chief of staff days after Republicans lost control of the US Congress in US midterm elections.
The president announced the extraordinary appointment on Friday, confirming that Susie Wiles – his current chief of staff, and the first woman to serve in the role – had been ousted.
In a social media ‌post, Trump called Miller, 41, “one of ​my most trusted advisors” and praised Wiles for doing “an ⁠outstanding job”. Miller will begin on Monday.
Wiles, 69, reportedly handed in her resignation on Thursday night and said in a social media post that serving Trump “has been the honor of a lifetime”.

Holding an umbrella, Trump emerged from the White House South Portico on Friday for a trip to Florida. “I wanted to make a change,” he said. “I think Susie’s done a very good job ... Stephen’s been great, and we’ve got to make moves.”
“Stephen’s been with me from the beginning. He gets it,” the president said. “Very good politically and he’s a very good man. He’ll do a great job. Great manager.”
Republicans hoping to succeed Trump in 2028 dissect midterm rout
Trump then boarded the Marine One helicopter, followed by Miller, secretary of state Marco Rubio and close aide Natalie Harp.
In a statement, Wiles added: “I’m so proud to have been a part of what we’ve accomplished together from securing our border and cutting taxes to strengthening our economy and putting America First.”
She said her commitment to “the President and the mission” will not change.

Miller’s appointment is the first sign of a shake-up at the White House following Republicans’ catastrophic defeat in the midterms. His record as a far-right firebrand implies that Trump is preparing for an aggressive fight against congressional Democrats’ oversight and investigations.

Chris Whipple, author of The Gatekeepers: How the White House Chiefs of Staff Define Every Presidency , told CNN: “It’s almost a declaration of war by Trump … He [Miller] only knows one gear and that’s full-throttle, full steam ahead over the cliff.”
David Axelrod, a veteran Democratic strategist, added on X : “For those who hoped the @POTUS might pivot to work with the incoming Congress, the appointment of Miller is a bucket of ICE cold water.”

Miller is one of the most polarising figures in the administration and one of Trump’s closest and longest-serving advisers, having joined his 2016 presidential campaign as a speechwriter. He is a former aide to the former senator Jeff Sessions of Alabama, who would go on to serve as Trump’s first attorney general.

In Trump’s first term, Miller was the driving force behind policies such as family separation and a travel ban on Muslim-majority countries. More than a hundred Democrats in Congress signed a letter to Trump calling Miller a “documented white nationalist” and demanding his removal.
A biography of Miller, written by journalist Jean Guerrero in 2020, was entitled Hatemonger.

Miller has served as deputy chief of staff since Trump’s return to the presidency in January 2025. He had been hugely influential in hardline immigration policies and demanding an end to birthright citizenship. He is also one Trump’s most ardent, outspoken and pugnacious defenders.

Appearing on Sean Hannity’s Fox News show on Monday, just before the midterms, Miller said of the president : “He saved America from a corrupt political class. He saved America from open borders. He saved America from countries that want the American way of life to end, from foreign adversaries, from domestic adversaries.”
body_zh: 美国总统确认现任幕僚长、第一位担任该职务的女性苏西·怀尔斯 (Susie Wiles) 将辞职
唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)最具争议的助手、全面打击移民行动的策划者史蒂芬·米勒(Stephen Miller)将在共和党在美国中期选举中失去对美国国会的控制权几天后成为他的新任白宫办公厅主任。
总统周五宣布了这一非凡任命，确认现任幕僚长、第一位担任该职位的女性苏西·怀尔斯 (Susie Wiles) 已被罢免。
在社交媒体帖子中，特朗普称 41 岁的米勒是“我最值得信赖的顾问之一”，并称赞怀尔斯做得“非常出色”。米勒将于周一开始。
据报道，69 岁的怀尔斯于周四晚递交了辞呈，并在社交媒体帖子中表示，为特朗普服务“是一生的荣幸”。
周五，特朗普撑着雨伞从白宫南门廊出来前往佛罗里达州。 “我想做出改变，”他说。 “我认为苏西做得很好......斯蒂芬很棒，我们必须采取行动。”
“斯蒂芬从一开始就和我在一起。他明白了，”总统说。 “政治上非常出色，他是一个非常好的人。他会做得很好。伟大的经理。”
希望在 2028 年接替特朗普的共和党人剖析中期选举溃败
随后，特朗普登上了海军陆战队一号直升机，米勒、国务卿马可·卢比奥和亲密助手娜塔莉·哈普紧随其后。
怀尔斯在一份声明中补充道：“我很自豪能够成为我们共同取得的成就的一部分，从保护边境安全、减税到加强我们的经济和实现美国优先。”
她表示，她对“总统和使命”的承诺不会改变。
米勒的任命是共和党在中期选举中惨败后白宫进行改组的第一个迹象。他作为极右煽动者的记录表明，特朗普正在准备积极对抗国会民主党的监督和调查。
《守门人：白宫幕僚长如何定义每一位总统》一书的作者克里斯·惠普尔 (Chris Whipple) 告诉 CNN：“这几乎是特朗普的宣战……他（米勒）只知道一个档位，而这就是全速前进、全速冲向悬崖。”
资深民主党策略师戴维·阿克塞尔罗德 (David Axelrod) 在 X 上补充道：“对于那些希望 @POTUS 转向与即将上任的国会合作的人来说，米勒的任命简直是 ICE 的一桶冷水。”
米勒是政府中最两极分化的人物之一，也是特朗普最亲密、任职时间最长的顾问之一，曾作为演讲撰稿人参加了他的 2016 年总统竞选活动。他是阿拉巴马州前参议员杰夫塞申斯的前助手，塞申斯后来担任特朗普的第一任司法部长。
在特朗普的第一个任期内，米勒是家庭分离和对穆斯林占多数国家的旅行禁令等政策的推动者。国会中的一百多名民主党人签署了一封致特朗普的信，称米勒是“有记录的白人民族主义者”，并要求将他免职。
记者 Jean Guerrero 在 2020 年撰写了米勒的传记，名为《Hatemonger》。
自特朗普于 2025 年 1 月重返总统职位以来，米勒一直担任副幕僚长。他在强硬的移民政策和要求结束与生俱来的公民身份方面发挥了巨大影响力。他也是特朗普最热情、最直言不讳、最好斗的捍卫者之一。
周一，就在中期选举之前，米勒在肖恩·汉尼提的福克斯新闻节目中谈到总统时说道：“他把美国从腐败的政治阶层手中拯救了出来。他把美国从开放的边界中拯救了出来。他把美国从那些想要结束美国生活方式的国家、外国对手和国内对手手中拯救了出来。”

body_en: US voters repudiated mass deportation campaign, but choice of new chief of staff shows Trump doesn’t care
On Tuesday, voters resoundingly rebuked Donald Trump and his brutal mass deportation campaign that sent military tanks and masked agents though residential streets.
But on Friday, the president doubled down. He named Stephen Miller – the architect of the administration’s most aggressive immigration policies – as his chief of staff.

It was never likely that Trump – who rose to political prominence on the promise that he would expel immigrants en masse from the US – would dampen his agenda, even after voters rejected Republican candidates up and down the ballot, near and far from the southern border, in blue and deep-red states.

But the elevation of Miller – a zealous, anti-immigrant crusader who has been by Trump’s side since the president’s first term – is an ominous signal that the deportation machine that Trump has built up over the past two years will be driving ahead at full speed.

Miller more than any single other person is responsible for unleashing a series of violent immigration raids across US cities this year and last, for sending hordes of masked agents in military gear through residential streets to round up undocumented immigrants. He has pushed the administration to all but shut down legal immigration as well. In his previous roles – as a deputy chief of staff and policy adviser – he has stuck close to Trump’s side and stoked the president’s most extreme instincts.

“The elevation of Stephen Miller to White House chief of staff signals a doubling down on the administration’s cruelest impulses,” said Faisal Al-Juburi, the co-chief executive of Raíces, a Texas-based humanitarian aid and immigration services non-profit. “Miller’s promotion guarantees an acceleration of mass deportations and of brute force unleashed within our neighborhoods.”

After immigration agents shot and killed Alex Pretti, a nurse, amid immigration raids in Minneapolis, it was Miller, according to the Wall Street Journal , who raised the idea that Trump could invoke the Insurrection Act to send in military troops.

It was Miller who came up with the legal framework of using the Alien Enemies Act to cast Venezuelan immigrants – including asylum seekers – as foreign terrorists associated with the Tren de Aragua cartel, and using that reasoning to expel them to a Salvadorian megaprison and to strike small Venezuelan boats .

During the first Trump administration, it was Miller who devised the “Muslim ban” restricting travel from Muslim-majority countries. It was he who designed the now-notorious zero tolerance policy of the first Trump administration – which separated more than 5,600 children from their parents and caregivers at the US-Mexico border. More recently, he’s pushed the administration to accelerate the deportation of undocumented children.

Miller, 41, who is himself the descendant of Jewish immigrants to the US and grew up in liberal Santa Monica, California, came to reject his home town , viewing California as a failed state that had been perverted by mass immigration. Eventually, he came to see immigration as a leftwing plot to undermine his vision of a traditional United States.

In more than a decade by Trump’s side, Miller has worked with the president to wrest extreme executive authority, to undermine Congress and the judiciary and defy oversight – in large part to advance his anti-immigrant campaign.
“He never backs down,” said Trump’s defense secretary Pete Hegseth in a congratulatory social media post, calling Miller a true patriot.

Democratic lawmakers who’ve re-taken control of Congress, governor’s offices and statehouses may have to spend much of the next two years bringing Miller’s ambitions to heel. Human rights activists and advocates on behalf of immigrants are immediately calling on congressmembers to do everything they can to stop Miller.

US representative Robert Garcia, the California Democrat who is poised to lead the House oversight committee next year, warned that Miller “should lawyer up” – promising to investigate him and his involvement in the administration’s mass deportation scheme.

Senator Alex Padilla said that if Trump was doubling down, “so will we”, promising to use “every tool at our disposal – oversight, investigations, subpoenas, and our leverage over federal funding – to expose this administration’s abuse of power and hold those responsible accountable”.

But even with full control of Congress, Democrats will likely have a limited ability to rein in the administration’s immigration enforcement agencies – which are bloated with $70bn in funding through 2029. Immigration and Customs Enforcement is poised to massively expand its workforce. Immigration arrests and detentions are already at an all-time high.

Miller, meanwhile, has shown a unique unwillingness to concede – in 2018, he reportedly sank a deal that would have gotten Trump $25bn funding for a border wall in exchange for a provision that would have provided permanent protection for undocumented immigrants who had come to the US as children.

It hasn’t seemed to faze him that the administration’s policies have alienated the coalition of voters who elected Trump into office in 2024 – including a large contingency of Latino voters. And he is unlikely to be moved by voters’ backlash against the Trump administration’s most extreme policies.
body_zh: 美国选民否认大规模驱逐运动，但新任幕僚长的选择表明特朗普并不关心
周二，选民强烈谴责唐纳德·特朗普及其残酷的大规模驱逐运动，该运动将军用坦克和蒙面特工派遣到住宅街道上。
但周五，总统加倍努力。他任命史蒂芬·米勒（Stephen Miller）——政府最激进的移民政策的设计者——为他的幕僚长。
特朗普 — — 由于承诺将大批移民驱逐出美国而获得政治声望 — — 即便在蓝州和深红州的选民在选票上上下下、在远离南部边境的地方拒绝了共和党候选人之后，他也不太可能抑制自己的议程。
但米勒 — — 一位热心的反移民斗士，自特朗普第一任期以来一直站在特朗普一边 — — 的升职是一个不祥的信号，表明特朗普在过去两年建立的驱逐机器将全速前进。
米勒对今年和去年在美国各城市发动的一系列暴力移民袭击负有最大的责任，他派出大批携带军事装备的蒙面特工穿过住宅街道围捕无证移民。他敦促政府几乎禁止合法移民。在他之前担任副幕僚长和政策顾问期间，他一直站在特朗普一边，并激发了总统最极端的本能。
“斯蒂芬·米勒升任白宫办公厅主任，标志着政府更加残酷的冲动，”总部位于得克萨斯州的人道主义援助和移民服务非营利组织 Raíces 的联席首席执行官费萨尔·朱布里 (Faisal Al-Juburi) 表示。 “米勒的晋升保证了大规模驱逐和在我们社区内释放暴力的加速。”
据《华尔街日报》报道，在明尼阿波利斯的移民突击搜查中，移民探员枪杀了护士亚历克斯·普雷蒂后，米勒提出了特朗普可以援引《叛乱法》派遣军队的想法。
米勒提出了利用《外国敌人法》将委内瑞拉移民（包括寻求庇护者）视为与特伦·德·阿拉瓜卡特尔有关联的外国恐怖分子的法律框架，并利用这一推理将他们驱逐到萨尔瓦多的巨型监狱并袭击委内瑞拉的小型船只。
在特朗普第一届政府期间，米勒制定了“穆斯林禁令”，限制来自穆斯林占多数的国家的旅行。正是他设计了第一届特朗普政府现在臭名昭著的零容忍政策，该政策将 5,600 多名儿童与他们的父母和看护者在美墨边境分开。最近，他敦促政府加速驱逐无证儿童。
41 岁的米勒本人是美国犹太移民的后裔，在自由派的加利福尼亚州圣莫尼卡长大，他开始拒绝自己的家乡，认为加利福尼亚州是一个因大规模移民而堕落的失败州。最终，他开始将移民视为左翼阴谋，破坏他对传统美国的愿景。
在特朗普身边的十多年来，米勒一直与总统合作，夺取极端行政权力，削弱国会和司法机构，藐视监督 — — 在很大程度上是为了推进他的反移民运动。
“他从不退缩，”特朗普的国防部长皮特·赫格斯在社交媒体上发帖表示祝贺，称米勒是真正的爱国者。
重新控制国会、州长办公室和州议会的民主党议员可能不得不在未来两年的大部分时间里让米勒的野心屈服。人权活动家和移民倡导者立即呼吁国会议员尽一切努力阻止米勒。
准备明年领导众议院监督委员会的加州民主党众议员罗伯特·加西亚警告说，米勒“应该请律师”——承诺调查他以及他参与政府大规模驱逐计划的情况。
参议员亚历克斯·帕迪拉表示，如果特朗普加倍努力，“我们也会加倍努力”，并承诺使用“我们可以使用的一切工具——监督、调查、传票以及我们对联邦资金的影响力——来揭露本届政府滥用权力的行为，并追究责任人的责任”。
但即使完全控制国会，民主党控制政府移民执法机构的能力也可能有限——到 2029 年，这些机构的资金将达到 700 亿美元。移民和海关执法机构准备大规模扩大劳动力。移民逮捕和拘留数量已经达到历史最高水平。
与此同时，米勒表现出了独特的不愿让步的态度——据报道，2018年，他否决了一项协议，该协议本来可以让特朗普为边境墙提供250亿美元的资金，以换取一项为儿童时期来到美国的无证移民提供永久保护的条款。
政府的政策疏远了 2024 年选举特朗普上台的选民联盟 — — 其中包括大量拉丁裔选民，这似乎并没有让他感到困扰。他不太可能因选民对特朗普政府最极端政策的强烈反对而感动。

body_en: Susie Wiles exits White House as Trump ousts another woman from key role | Donald Trump
Wiles thanks president for ‘honor of a lifetime’ as departure leaves behind overwhelmingly male leadership team

Donald Trump on Friday said Susie Wiles, the first woman to serve as White House chief of staff, will leave her post, a major shake-up of his inner circle that comes amid a steady exodus of senior female officials from his administration.

The president announced her ouster – and her replacement, by the immigration hardliner Stephen Miller – in a post on Truth Social, days after a sweeping blue wave gave Democrats control of both chambers of Congress in the midterm elections. Wiles’s departure leaves behind an overwhelmingly male leadership team.
“I wanted to make a change,” he told reporters on Friday. “I think Susie’s done a very good job … Stephen’s been great and we’ve got to make moves.”
Stephen Miller, architect of Trump’s immigration crackdown, to become White House chief of staff

Wiles, who reportedly handed in her resignation on Thursday night, said her role as chief of staff “has been the honor of a lifetime,” adding: “I’m so proud to have been a part of what we’ve accomplished together, from securing our border and cutting taxes to strengthening our economy and putting America first.”

Wiles’s exit follows a string of high-profile resignations and dismissals of women in the Trump administration. In recent months, White House press secretary Katie Zacharia was ousted just five days after taking up the role, while former homeland security secretary Kristi Noem and former attorney general Pam Bondi were also dismissed.
Former national intelligence director Tulsi Gabbard reportedly resigned under pressure, while Kimberly Guilfoyle, the former US ambassador to Greece, has also departed her post.

As high-ranking women left the administration, Wiles, diagnosed with breast cancer, stayed put, with Trump even claiming at one point: “She’s going to be here for a long time”. Wiles announced in September that she was cancer-free.

Just a day before Trump’s announcement of Wiles’s ouster, Harmeet Dhillon, a staunch Trump ally and controversial head of the justice department’s civil rights division, also resigned , marking yet another high-profile woman’s departure from the Trump administration.

Dhillon’s resignation comes amid expectations Democrats will use their majority in Congress to investigate federal agencies under Trump, including the US justice department, which has repeatedly been accused of being weaponized by the administration to pursue Trump’s own political enemies.

Other justice department officials have also since resigned amid the major post-midterm personnel shakeup, including John Eisenberg, the assistant attorney general for national security, as well as Jason Reding Quiñones, a key attorney that led inquiries into Trump’s rivals.
Only a handful of women remain in Trump’s cabinet, including agriculture secretary Brooke Rollins and Kelly Loeffler, head of the Small Business Administration.

Natalie Harp, the 35-year-old political aide, remains a frequent presence by the president’s side at public events. Harp has previously written letters to the president in which she described him as “my guardian and protector” .
body_zh: 特朗普罢免另一位女性关键职务，苏西·怀尔斯退出白宫唐纳德·特朗普
怀尔斯感谢总统“一生的荣誉”，因为他的离开留下了绝大多数男性领导团队
唐纳德·特朗普周五表示，第一位担任白宫办公厅主任的女性苏西·威尔斯将离职，这是他的核心圈子的一次重大改组，而其政府中的高级女性官员正在不断流失。
就在几天前，席卷而来的蓝色浪潮让民主党在中期选举中控制了国会参众两院，几天后，总统在《真相社会》(Truth Social) 的一篇文章中宣布将她罢免，并由移民强硬派斯蒂芬·米勒 (Stephen Miller) 接替她。怀尔斯的离开留下了一支以男性为主的领导团队。
“我想做出改变，”他周五告诉记者。 “我认为苏西做得很好......斯蒂芬很棒，我们必须采取行动。”
特朗普移民镇压策划者斯蒂芬·米勒将出任白宫办公厅主任
据报道，怀尔斯于周四晚上递交了辞呈，她表示，担任幕僚长的角色“是我一生的荣幸”，并补充道：“我很自豪能够成为我们共同取得的成就的一部分，从保护我们的边境和减税到加强我们的经济和把美国放在第一位。”
怀尔斯退出之前，特朗普政府中出现了一系列备受瞩目的女性辞职和解雇事件。近几个月来，白宫新闻秘书凯蒂·扎卡里亚(Katie Zacharia)上任仅五天就被罢免，前国土安全部长克里斯蒂·诺姆(Kristi Noem)和前司法部长帕姆·邦迪(Pam ​​Bondi)也被解雇。
据报道，前国家情报总监图尔西·加巴德(Tulsi Gabbard)迫于压力辞职，前美国驻希腊大使金伯利·吉尔福伊尔(Kimberly Guilfoyle)也已离职。
随着高级女性离开政府，被诊断出患有乳腺癌的怀尔斯留在原地，特朗普甚至一度声称：“她将在这里待很长时间”。怀尔斯九月宣布她的癌症已痊愈。
就在特朗普宣布罢免怀尔斯的前一天，特朗普的坚定盟友、备受争议的司法部民权部门负责人哈米特·迪隆也辞职，这标志着又一位备受瞩目的女性离开特朗普政府。
迪隆辞职之际，人们预计民主党将利用其在国会的多数席位来调查特朗普领导下的联邦机构，其中包括美国司法部，该部门一再被指控被政府武器化以追捕特朗普自己的政敌。
此后，其他司法部官员也在中期选举后的重大人事变动中辞职，其中包括负责国家安全的助理司法部长约翰·艾森伯格，以及领导对特朗普竞争对手进行调查的重要律师杰森·雷丁·奎诺内斯。
特朗普内阁中只剩下少数女性，包括农业部长布鲁克·罗林斯和小企业管理局局长凯利·洛夫勒。
35 岁的政治助手娜塔莉·哈普 (Natalie Harp) 仍然经常出现在总统身边出席公共活动。哈普此前曾写信给总统，称他为“我的监护人和保护者”。

title_en: No one knows how many ballots are outstanding in Mississippi's Senate race

summary: The razor-thin margin between GOP Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith and Democrat Scott Colom is shining a light on an election process in Mississippi that is among the slowest and most decentralized in the U.S.
summary_zh: 共和党参议员辛迪·海德·史密斯 (Cindy Hyde-Smith) 和民主党参议员斯科特·科洛姆 (Scott Colom) 之间的微弱优势让密西西比州的选举进程焕然一新。
body_en: Mississippi Senate: Exact tally of affidavit ballots unknown : NPR

Mississippi Senate: Exact tally of affidavit ballots unknown The razor-thin margin between GOP Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith and Democrat Scott Colom is shining a light on an election process in Mississippi that is among the slowest and most decentralized in the U.S.

Two Madison County election commissioners inspect an affidavit ballot envelope on Thursday in Canton, Miss. The state's razor-thin U.S. Senate race is shining a spotlight on Mississippi's election processes. Rogelio V. Solis/Getty Images hide caption
In Mississippi's too-close-to-call U.S. Senate race, every ballot matters.
But no one can say for sure how many ballots there are left to count.

The razor-thin margin between incumbent Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith and Democratic challenger Scott Colom is shining a light on an election process in Mississippi that is among the slowest and most decentralized in the country. It also doesn't have any provisions for recounts .
"Mississippi is not a model of election administration," said Michael Morse, a law professor at the University of Pennsylvania who studies voting.
As of mid-afternoon Friday, more than 2,000 votes separated the two Senate candidates. But information about exactly how many ballots were outstanding was hard to come by.

The Colom campaign said late Tuesday it was aware of more than 15,000 provisional ballots , which require verification before they're counted. And the chair of the state Republican Party said Thursday he thought there were 20,000 outstanding ballots, including potential absentee votes that can legally be received by officials until Nov. 10 if they were postmarked by Election Day.

Mississippi's top voting official, Republican Secretary of State Michael Watson, said counties run their own elections, and even his office didn't know how many provisionals were left to count. He said midday Friday over 9,000 of them had been processed.

"Until we have the certified results, the individual counties will be the best source of the latest and most up-to-date information," Watson said in a statement. There are 82 counties in Mississippi, and they are not required to transmit election results to the state until next week.
Morse said he was shocked by the lack of good information available for such a high-profile race.
"Right now I would love to know a lot of things about the process and I am struggling to figure out what is unfolding here," Morse said. "I cannot tell you basic things."
Mississippi has a relatively high rate of provisional ballots

What is becoming clear is that the rate of provisional ballots, which are called affidavit ballots in Mississippi, may end up being among the highest in the country this election cycle. Those ballots are cast by people whose eligibility is questionable, according to local officials, so those votes are segregated and officials decide on a case-by-case basis whether they will be counted.
If the Colom campaign's estimate of 15,000 affidavit ballots holds true, that would represent roughly 1.5% of the total ballots cast in the Senate race, according to unofficial results.

In the last midterm year, 2022, just four states had a provisional ballot rate higher than that, according to federal data . And Mississippi looks to have a provisional rate close to double of that in North Carolina this year, based on the preliminary data in both states.

密西西比州参议院：宣誓选票的确切统计未知共和党参议员辛迪·海德·史密斯和民主党人斯科特·科洛姆之间的微弱优势让密西西比州的选举进程成为美国最缓慢、最分散的选举进程之一。
周四，两名麦迪逊县选举专员在密西西比州坎顿检查宣誓选票信封。该州的美国参议员竞选微弱，成为密西西比州选举进程的焦点。 Rogelio V. Solis/Getty Images 隐藏标题栏
在密西西比州势均力敌的美国参议院竞选中，每一张选票都很重要。
但没有人能确定还剩下多少张选票需要清点。
现任共和党参议员辛迪·海德·史密斯 (Cindy Hyde-Smith) 和民主党挑战者斯科特·科洛姆 (Scott Colom) 之间的微弱优势凸显了密西西比州的选举进程，该州是该国选举进程最慢、权力最分散的地区之一。它也没有任何重新计票的规定。
“密西西比州不是选举管理的典范，”宾夕法尼亚大学研究投票的法学教授迈克尔·莫尔斯说。
截至周五下午三点左右，两名参议院候选人的票数已超过 2000 张。但很难获得关于到底有多少张选票尚未完成的信息。
科罗姆竞选团队周二晚间表示，他们知道有超过 15,000 张临时选票，需要在计票前进行验证。该州共和党主席周四表示，他认为还有 20,000 张未完成的选票，其中包括潜在的缺席选票，如果这些选票在选举日之前盖上邮戳，官员们可以在 11 月 10 日之前合法收到这些选票。
密西西比州最高投票官员、共和党国务卿迈克尔·沃森表示，各县自行选举，就连他的办公室也不知道还有多少临时候选人需要统计。他说，周五中午，其中 9,000 多份已得到处理。
沃森在一份声明中表示：“在我们获得经过认证的结果之前，各个县将成为最新信息的最佳来源。”密西西比州有 82 个县，下周之前它们不需要将选举结果传送给该州。
莫尔斯表示，他对如此引人注目的比赛缺乏良好的信息感到震惊。
莫尔斯说：“现在我很想了解有关这个过程的很多事情，但我正在努力弄清楚这里正在发生什么。” “我不能告诉你基本的事情。”
密西西比州的临时选票率相对较高
越来越清楚的是，临时选票（在密西西比州被称为宣誓选票）的投票率最终可能会成为本次选举周期全国最高的选票之一。据当地官员称，这些选票是由资格存疑的人投票的，因此这些选票是分开的，官员们会根据具体情况决定是否将其计算在内。
根据非官方结果，如果科罗姆竞选团队估计的 15,000 张宣誓选票成立，这将约占参议院竞选总选票的 1.5%。
根据联邦数据，在上个中期选举年（即 2022 年）中，只有四个州的临时选票率高于该数字。根据这两个州的初步数据，密西西比州今年的临时利率似乎接近北卡罗来纳州的两倍。

body_en: Man with guns arrested near White House, told Secret Service he planned to kill Trump, DHS says - CBS News

An undocumented immigrant armed with several weapons was taken into custody within blocks of the White House Thursday night after he allegedly told Secret Service officers that he was planning an attempt on President Trump's life, the U.S. Department of Homeland Security said.

The suspect, identified as Ronny Yordrix Guanipa Chrinos of Venezuela, was arrested on three counts each of unlawful transportation of a firearm, carrying unregistered firearms and carrying unregistered ammunition, along with one count each of possession of certain dangerous weapons, carrying a pistol without a license, unauthorized use of a motor vehicle, theft and receiving stolen property, DHS said in a news release Friday.

Secret Service officers observed the suspect acting suspiciously in his vehicle and approached him while he was parked on Constitution Avenue, DHS said. A law enforcement source told CBS News the incident took place in the 1600 block of Constitution Avenue NW, near the Ellipse.
When officers confronted the suspect, DHS said, he allegedly told them that he had heard voices in his head telling him to come to Washington, D.C., and assassinate Mr. Trump.
The Secret Service officers learned the suspect's vehicle had been reported stolen, DHS said, and the suspect allegedly admitted there were weapons in the vehicle.
When officers searched the vehicle, they found three firearms, including a rifle, as well as dozens of rounds of ammunition, according to DHS, which released a photo of the seized items.

"This is the latest example of Secret Service personnel relying on extensive training and experience to deescalate a volatile situation that posed an imminent threat to our protectees and other Americans," Secret Service Director Sean Curran said in a statement.
DHS said the suspect entered the U.S. through Texas in March 2024 and was arrested by U.S. Border Patrol, but was later released. It was not immediately clear if he had an attorney.

"Thanks to our brave Secret Service officers, this illegal alien with three firearms in his vehicle was arrested near the White House before he could harm anyone," Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said in a separate statement.

Mr. Trump has been the target of multiple assassination attempts since entering political life, most notably a shooting at a rally in Butler, Pennsylvania, during his second presidential campaign in July 2024 in which a sniper opened fire from the roof of a nearby building, killing one attendee and wounding Mr. Trump and two others.

In April, chaos broke out when a gunman breached security during the White House Correspondents' Dinner at the Washington Hilton Hotel while Mr. Trump and first lady Melania Trump were in attendance. The suspect was arrested at the scene, and a Secret Service officer was wounded in the incident.

body_en: Man in custody after being found in vehicle near White House with guns | Washington DC
Ronny Yordrix Guanipa Chrinos arrested by secret service after telling officers voices told him to kill Donald Trump

The US secret service said a suspect has been taken into custody and charged after officers found him in a vehicle near the White House with multiple guns, claiming he heard voices in his head telling him to kill Donald Trump .

The arrest Thursday night happened after secret service officers approached a man “acting suspicious” in a parked car, according to a Homeland Security statement. US officials said the suspect – Ronny Yordrix Guanipa Chrinos – went on to describe voices in his head that were telling him to come to the nation’s capital and kill the Republican president.

Shortly after, officers discovered the suspect’s vehicle had been reported stolen and he had three firearms and dozens of rounds of ammunition. This is the latest in a series of arrests the secret service and other law enforcement agencies have made against individuals who have threatened Trump or his family members’ lives since he returned to office last year.

The statement described Chrinos as an immigrant from Venezuela who is in the country illegally after entering the US through Texas in March 2024. DHS said he had been charged and was in US Marshals Service custody.
The White House did not provide comment, instead referring to DHS and the US secret service.

title_en: The White House’s post-election shake-up: From the Politics Desk
title_zh: 白宫的选举后改组：来自政治部门
summary: In today’s edition, we dive into President Donald Trump’s decision to make a change at chief of staff. Plus, Kristen Welker examines how voters once again rejected the status quo.
summary_zh: 在今天的版本中，我们将深入探讨唐纳德·特朗普总统改变幕僚长的决定。另外，克里斯汀·韦尔克（Kristen Welker）研究了选民如何一次
body_en: Trump names Stephen Miller as new White House chief of staff after midterm losses
In today’s edition, we dive into President Donald Trump’s decision to make a change at chief of staff. Plus, Kristen Welker examines how voters once again rejected the status quo.
Trump names Stephen Miller his new chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles

President Donald Trump has turned to MAGA favorite Stephen Miller to lead the White House after Republicans got trounced in Tuesday’s midterm elections, losing both chambers of Congress by wide margins.

Trump announced the change at the top on Truth Social this afternoon, with Miller, his deputy chief of staff, taking over chief of staff duties from Susie Wiles on Monday. Wiles submitted her resignation Thursday night, according to a White House official.

The shift from Wiles, a longtime establishment figure in Florida and national political circles, to Miller, the hard-charging architect of the president’s mass-deportation campaign, sends a signal to a fractured Republican Party that Trump intends to strengthen ties to the MAGA base in his final two years in office. It also portends an even more contentious relationship with Democrats in Congress, who have demonized Miller for years.

“Miller knows the key issues and is a true believer — and he knows the ecosystem around the issues,” said Steve Bannon , a former senior Trump aide and host of ‘The War Room” podcast. “Stephen gets parachuted in and takes immediate control.”

On a recent phone call with an ally, Trump praised Miller as an aide who gets things done and doesn’t just tell him what he wants to hear. The ally said that Miller will be combative with Congress, particularly when it comes to any investigations Democrats point toward the administration.
“When the president says, ‘Do this,’ Stephen will do it, and he’ll leave bodies behind doing it,” the ally said.
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries , D-N.Y., who is widely expected to become speaker in January, called for Miller to be fired, not promoted.

“Stephen Miller is a dangerous xenophobe and reckless extremist who has American blood on his hands,” Jeffries wrote on X . “His presence in government should be eradicated like a malignant tumor. Fire him today.”
The midterms reveal a much larger slice of the electorate is up for grabs
We thought the 2024 presidential contest was a realignment election, one that would scramble political alliances and change the way both parties try to win for years to come.
It turns out that we were only right about the second half.

As the dust settles on the 2026 midterms, where Democrats made deep inroads in red states and districts to rack up historic gains in the House and Senate (with more key races still uncalled), one major takeaway is that the group of voters who aren’t strictly guided by pure partisanship is far larger than many may have thought.

Those same young, Latino and disaffected voters that helped power President Donald Trump ’s victory in 2024 swung dramatically back to Democrats two years later, underscoring that the last two elections weren’t realignments, but rejections of the status quo. After Trump campaigned on tackling rising inflation and bringing down costs, pre-election and exit polling this year makes clear these voters believe he didn’t keep his promises.
But just like these swing voters were not permanently a part of the GOP coalition after 2024, Democrats can’t take them for granted now.
It now falls to Democrats to figure out how to follow through with the mandate they were given in a divided government, and how to avoid self-inflicted damage from their own factionalism.

And Republicans will face a different, yet inextricably linked task — sifting through the wreckage of a disappointing election and figuring out the path forward, not unlike what Democrats faced after 2024.

Where both parties go next will shape the lame duck period before the new Congress is sown in, the legislative goals both parties will pursue over the next two years, and, of course, the 2028 presidential election.
body_zh: 中期选举失利后，特朗普任命斯蒂芬·米勒为新任白宫办公厅主任
在今天的版本中，我们将深入探讨唐纳德·特朗普总统改变幕僚长的决定。此外，克里斯汀·韦尔克（Kristen Welker）研究了选民如何再次拒绝现状。
特朗普任命斯蒂芬·米勒为新任幕僚长，接替苏西·怀尔斯
共和党在周二的中期选举中惨败，以大幅优势输掉国会两院后，唐纳德·特朗普总统转向最喜爱的斯蒂芬·米勒来领导白宫。
特朗普今天下午在《真相社会》上宣布了这一高层变动，他的副幕僚长米勒周一从苏西·威尔斯手中接替了幕僚长职务。据白宫官员称，怀尔斯周四晚提交了辞呈。
从佛罗里达州和全国政界的长期建制人物怀尔斯到总统大规模驱逐运动的强硬策划者米勒的转变，向分裂的共和党发出了一个信号，即特朗普打算在任期的最后两年加强与“让美国再次伟大”基地的联系。这也预示着与国会民主党人的关系更具争议性，多年来民主党人一直妖魔化米勒。
特朗普前高级助手、《作战室》播客主持人史蒂夫·班农 (Steve Bannon) 表示：“米勒了解关键问题，是一个真正的信徒，而且他了解这些问题周围的生态系统。斯蒂芬跳伞进入并立即掌控局势。”
在最近与一位盟友的电话中，特朗普称赞米勒是一位能把事情做好的助手，而不仅仅是告诉他想听的话。这位盟友表示，米勒将对国会表现出好斗的态度，特别是在民主党针对政府进行的任何调查方面。
这位盟友说：“当总统说‘做这个’时，斯蒂芬就会这么做，而且他会留下尸体。”
人们普遍预计将在一月份成为众议院议长的纽约州众议院少数党领袖哈基姆·杰弗里斯 (Hakeem Jeffries) 呼吁解雇米勒，而不是升职。
杰弗里斯在 X 上写道：“斯蒂芬·米勒是一个危险的仇外者和鲁莽的极端分子，他的手上沾满了美国人的鲜血。” “他在政府中的存在应该像恶性肿瘤一样被根除。今天就解雇他。”
中期选举显示，更大一部分选民有待争夺
我们认为 2024 年总统竞选是一场重新结盟的选举，这场选举将扰乱政治联盟并改变双方在未来几年试图获胜的方式。
事实证明我们只对下半场的预测是正确的。
随着 2026 年中期选举的尘埃落定，民主党在红色州和选区取得了深入进展，在参众两院取得了历史性进展（还有更多关键竞选尚未宣布），一个主要的收获是，不受纯粹党派偏见严格引导的选民群体远比许多人想象的要大。
那些帮助唐纳德·特朗普总统在 2024 年获胜的年轻、拉丁裔和心怀不满的选民在两年后戏剧性地转向了民主党，这突显出最近两次选举不是重新结盟，而是对现状的拒绝。在特朗普竞选时主张应对通胀上升和降低成本后，今年的选前和出口民意调查清楚地表明，这些选民认为他没有信守承诺。
但就像这些摇摆不定的选民在 2024 年之后不会永久成为共和党联盟的一部分一样，民主党现在也不能认为他们是理所当然的。
现在，民主党人必须弄清楚如何履行在分裂的政府中赋予他们的使命，以及如何避免因派系斗争而给自己造成伤害。
共和党将面临一项不同但又密不可分的任务——清理令人失望的选举的废墟并找出前进的道路，这与民主党在 2024 年之后面临的情况没有什么不同。
两党接下来的走向将决定新国会成立之前的跛脚鸭时期、两党在未来两年追求的立法目标，当然还有 2028 年总统选举。

title_en: Trump's global health strategy is emerging. What will the Democratic Congress say?
title_zh: 特朗普的全球卫生战略正在形成。民主党国会会说什么？
summary: The Trump Administration has ushered in a fundamental shift in the U.S. approach to global health aid. How will the newly elected Democratic Congress weigh in?
summary_zh: 特朗普政府使美国对全球卫生援助的方式发生了根本性转变。新当选的民主党国会将如何
body_en: At an October meeting, signed copies of the health cooperation memorandum of understanding between the U.S. and Zambia are displayed by U.S. Embassy Chargé d'Affaires Mich Coker (left) and Zambia's Minister of Finance and National Planning Situmbeko Musokotwane (center). Minister of Health Roma Chilengi (right) applauds. U.S Embassy in Zambia hide caption

By all appearances, it was a classic government ceremony. Officials in suits. Big black chairs around a wooden table. A cluster of microphones. It happened on October 8 in Lusaka, Zambia. Amid applause, U.S. and Zambian officials signed a global health agreement, called a Memorandum of Understanding or MOU.
But Mich Coker — the Chargé d'Affaires at the U.S. Embassy in Zambia — said this agreement was anything but classic.

"This MOU represents a fundamental shift," he said, speaking at the signing ceremony . He explained that the relationship between the two countries was moving "from a traditional donor-recipient model to a true partnership, one grounded in Zambian leadership, in Zambian ownership and in shared accountability."
Global health experts on all sides of the political spectrum and all over the world agree with Coker that there's been a fundamental shift in the U.S. approach to global health.
"The shift that's currently unfolding is very large and it's very rapid," says Janeen Madan Keller, acting co-director of the Global Health Program at the Center for Global Development.

The story of this fundamental shift starts at the beginning of the second Trump Administration with months of global health turmoil — Madan Keller and other experts say — but has given way to a clearer strategy. One with big goals, a short timeline and a lot less transparency than what came before.
Here is a look at where things stand now and how a Congress controlled by the Democratic Party might impact the new landscape.
President Trump's second term started dramatically. When he dismantled USAID (the U.S. Agency for International Development), citing alleged " fraud, waste and abuse ," everything changed overnight.

"It is a period that is best described as chaos," says Madan Keller. The repercussions were massive and immediate, she says, "for people and communities in some of the poorest countries of the world."

Clinics shut down suddenly. Patients ran out of HIV medications. In Zambia, as well as a number of other countries, many patients who relied on U.S.-supported clinics and programs faced tons of uncertainty and, often, dire health consequences .
"For the first half of 2025, there was a complete upheaval," says Jennifer Kates , senior vice president and director of global and public health policy at KFF.

Next came a new stage in the history of U.S. foreign aid. "Starting over the summer of 2025 and going into September, there actually was a sort of step back to develop an actual strategy and a plan," says Kates.

What emerged from the State Department was the America First Global Health Strategy with the stated goal of making "America safer, stronger, and more prosperous." The main way this strategy is being implemented is through agreements with individual countries. In the past, the U.S. had done more work through large international organizations or local non-governmental organizations.

Experts say one defining feature of these agreements is that they are transactional. For example, in Zambia "there was a massive scandal because activists were able to show that the agreement was planning to condition access to [U.S. global health] funding on access to [Zambia's] copper and rare earth minerals," says Asia Russell , executive director of the HIV/AIDS advocacy organization Health GAP. Her organization helped expose this situation.

While the part of the agreement about minerals was separated from the global health agreement after the public outcry in Zambia, many of the global health agreements do require the recipient country to share data such as pathogen information.

Speaking at the signing ceremony in Zambia, Coker ticked off some of the top priorities in the new strategy, including that recipient countries increase their financial contributions to health in the years ahead and that they are transitioned off aid in the near future.

He said in the Zambian MOU, the U.S. would pay $1.5 billion over five years "with Zambia simultaneously committing to increase its own domestic health expenditures by $975 million. We are charting a path toward a stronger, more self-reliant health system."
Another priority has been building up a country's own health infrastructure — and not a parallel system run by non-profits and NGOs.
body_zh: 在 10 月份的一次会议上，美国大使馆临时代办 Mich Coker（左）和赞比亚财政和国家规划部长 Situmbeko Musokotwane（中）展示了美国和赞比亚之间签署的卫生合作谅解备忘录的副本。卫生部长 Roma Chilengi（右）鼓掌。美国驻赞比亚大使馆隐藏标题栏
从表面上看，这是一场典型的政府仪式。穿西装的官员。木桌周围有黑色的大椅子。一组麦克风。这件事发生在10月8日的赞比亚卢萨卡。在掌声中，美国和赞比亚官员签署了一项全球卫生协议，称为谅解备忘录或谅解备忘录。
但美国驻赞比亚大使馆临时代办米奇·科克表示，这项协议绝非经典。
“这份谅解备忘录代表着根本性的转变，”他在签字仪式上说道。他解释说，两国之间的关系正在“从传统的捐助者-受援者模式转变为真正的伙伴关系，这种伙伴关系以赞比亚的领导、赞比亚的所有权和共同的责任为基础”。
世界各地政治派别的全球卫生专家都同意科克的观点，即美国对全球卫生的态度发生了根本性转变。
全球发展中心全球健康项目代理联席主任珍宁·马丹·凯勒 (Janeen Madan Keller) 表示：“目前正在发生的转变规模非常大，而且速度非常快。”
马丹·凯勒和其他专家表示，这一根本性转变的故事始于特朗普第二届政府上任之初，当时全球卫生领域经历了数月的动荡，但现在已经让位于更清晰的战略。与以前相比，它的目标远大，时间表较短，透明度也低得多。
以下是目前的情况以及民主党控制的国会可能如何影响新格局。
特朗普总统的第二任期戏剧性地开始了。当他以所谓的“欺诈、浪费和滥用”为由解散美国国际开发署（USAID）时，一切都在一夜之间发生了变化。
“这是一个用混乱来形容的时期，”马丹·凯勒说。她说，“对于世界上一些最贫穷国家的人民和社区来说”，影响是巨大而直接的。
诊所突然关闭。患者的艾滋病药物用完了。在赞比亚以及其他一些国家，许多依赖美国支持的诊所和项目的患者面临着大量的不确定性，而且往往面临着可怕的健康后果。
KFF 高级副总裁兼全球和公共卫生政策总监 Jennifer Kates 表示：“2025 年上半年发生了彻底的剧变。”
接下来，美国对外援助的历史进入了一个新阶段。 “从 2025 年夏季开始到 9 月，实际上需要退一步来制定实际的战略和计划，”凯特说。
美国国务院提出了“美国第一全球健康战略”，其既定目标是“让美国更安全、更强大、更繁荣”。该战略实施的主要方式是通过与各个国家达成协议。过去，美国更多是通过大型国际组织或地方非政府组织做的工作。
专家表示，这些协议的一个显着特征是它们是交易性的。例如，在赞比亚，“发生了一场大规模丑闻，因为活动人士能够证明该协议计划以获取[赞比亚]铜和稀土矿产为条件来获得[美国全球卫生]资金，”艾滋病毒/艾滋病倡导组织健康差距（Health GAP）执行董事阿莎·拉塞尔（Asia Russell）说。她的组织帮助揭露了这一情况。
尽管在赞比亚引起公众强烈抗议后，有关矿物的协议部分从全球卫生协议中分离出来，但许多全球卫生协议确实要求受援国共享病原体信息等数据。
科克在赞比亚举行的签字仪式上发表讲话，列举了新战略中的一些首要任务，包括受援国在未来几年增加对卫生的财政捐助，并在不久的将来停止援助。
他表示，在赞比亚谅解备忘录中，美国将在五年内支付 15 亿美元，“赞比亚同时承诺将其国内卫生支出增加 9.75 亿美元。我们正在规划一条通往更强大、更自力更生的卫生系统的道路。”
另一个优先事项是建立一个国家自己的卫生基础设施，而不是由非营利组织和非政府组织运营的并行系统。

title_en: Houston to limit police cooperation with federal immigration authorities
title_zh: 休斯顿限制警方与联邦移民当局的合作
summary: Mayor said only immigrants that ‘pose a danger’ would be referred to ICE, after Democrats gain control of governor’s seat The mayor of Houston on Friday said the city would limit cooperation with federal immigration authorities, heralding “a new model” of immi
summary_zh: 市长表示，在民主党控制州长席位后，只有“构成危险”​​的移民才会被移交给 ICE。
body_en: Mayor said only immigrants that ‘pose a danger’ would be referred to ICE, after Democrats gain control of governor’s seat

The mayor of Houston on Friday said the city would limit cooperation with federal immigration authorities, heralding “a new model” of immigration enforcement after Democrats won power in Texas for the first time in decades.
Houston’s mayor, John Whitmire, said the city would go after immigrants “that pose a danger, not those that are going about their family business, work and education”.

A traffic incident “will not even [trigger immigration enforcement] … You write a citation or you warn them and they go about their way. No contact with [Immigration and Customs Enforcement] over nonviolent, non-jailable offenses. It reduces the fear and anxiety.”
The move by the nation’s fourth-largest city is one of the first steps to curb ICE’s powers since Tuesday’s midterm elections.
‘Hunted like animals’: inside Trump’s war on the people who build America
In July, ICE agents shot and killed Lorenzo Salgado Araujo during a traffic stop in Houston while reportedly looking for other individuals.

The shooting rattled residents of the Magnolia Park neighborhood in Houston, where the shooting occurred. It was also another blow to the embattled housing construction industry in Texas, which has been losing skilled, experienced workers at a high volume and high rates.

“We feel it on a level we can’t even describe,” a neighbor who declined to share his name for fear of retaliation told the Guardian in July . “Everybody knows that what happened is wrong. How will we not stand with our people, stand behind them, especially when something so vicious and ugly happened?”

Under the mayor’s new directive, Houston police should contact ICE only if the person it stops is arrested on a charge that is subject to jailing or if ICE issues an administrative warrant, which is an order signed by a senior ICE official indicating that the person is wanted by immigration officials.

“The fact that a person is, or is suspected to be, subject to immigration enforcement shall not, by itself, be a basis to contact ICE, to prolong any detention, or to take any person into or hold any person in custody,” the two-page order states.
Spokespersons for ICE did not immediately respond to an email seeking comment on the mayor’s announcement.
In October, an ICE agent struck an individual with their vehicle during a pursuit of a different suspect whose family noted he died years ago.

A grand jury indicted ICE officer Mario Alberto Morales on a charge of aggravated assault with a deadly weapon. Prosecutors say Morales intentionally rammed his car into Miguel Parra Hernandez, whose leg was broken. ICE has asserted that Parra Hernandez ran in front of the vehicle, an account that prosecutors say is contradicted by video.

Despite a one-time $75bn infusion from Congress, ICE remains heavily dependent on local police to find people subject to deportation and turn them over. It has done so partly by signing about 2,600 agreements – many in Texas – to deputize local police and other state and local agencies to enforce immigration laws. Texas has been a primary target for ICE arrests.

Texas’s governor, Greg Abbott, has closely aligned the state with the Trump administration to collaborate on enforcing federal immigration laws. He lost his bid for a fourth term to Democrat Gina Hinojosa.
Fiel, an immigrant-rights group in Houston that has been working with the family of Parra Hernandez, planned to hold a press conference on Friday afternoon in light of the announcement.
“Today Houston won. The Houston city council had already decided this months ago,” said Cesar Espinosa, executive director of Fiel Houston, adding that it was time to follow through.
body_zh: 市长表示，在民主党控制州长席位后，只有“构成危险”​​的移民才会被移交给 ICE
休斯顿市长周五表示，该市将限制与联邦移民当局的合作，在民主党几十年来首次赢得德克萨斯州权力后，预示着移民执法的“新模式”。
休斯顿市长约翰·惠特米尔表示，该市将追捕“构成危险的移民，而不是那些从事家族生意、工作和教育的移民”。
交通事故“甚至不会[触发移民执法]……你写一张传票或警告他们，他们就会按自己的方式行事。不会因非暴力、不可入狱的犯罪行为而与[移民和海关执法部门]接触。这减少了恐惧和焦虑。”
美国第四大城市的此举是自周二中期选举以来遏制 ICE 权力的首批措施之一。
“像动物一样被猎杀”：特朗普对美国建设者的战争
7 月，ICE 特工在休斯敦的一个交通站点开枪打死了洛伦佐·萨尔加多·阿劳霍 (Lorenzo Salgado Araujo)，据报道当时他正在寻找其他人。
这起枪击事件让枪击事件发生地休斯敦木兰公园附近的居民感到不安。这也是对德克萨斯州陷入困境的住房建筑行业的又一次打击，该行业一直在大量高比例地流失熟练、经验丰富的工人。
“我们的感受甚至无法描述，”一位因担心遭到报复而拒绝透露姓名的邻居七月份告诉《卫报》。 “每个人都知道所发生的事情是错误的。我们怎么会不与我们的人民站在一起，站在他们身后，尤其是当发生如此邪恶和丑陋的事情时？”
根据市长的新指令，休斯敦警方只有在拦截的人因可判处监禁的罪名被捕或 ICE 发出行政令（由 ICE 高级官员签署的命令，表明该人受到移民官员通缉）时才应联系 ICE。
这份长达两页的命令指出，“某人正在或被怀疑受到移民执法的事实本身不应成为联系 ICE、延长拘留或拘留任何人的依据。”
ICE 发言人没有立即回复寻求对市长声明发表评论的电子邮件。
10 月，一名 ICE 特工在追捕另一名嫌疑人时用车辆撞死了一名男子，该嫌疑人的家人称该嫌疑人多年前已去世。
大陪审团以使用致命武器严重袭击罪名起诉 ICE 官员马里奥·阿尔贝托·莫拉莱斯 (Mario Alberto Morales)。检察官称，莫拉莱斯故意将自己的汽车撞向米格尔·帕拉·埃尔南德斯，导致其腿骨折。 ICE 声称帕拉·埃尔南德斯跑到了车辆前面，检察官称这一说法与视频相矛盾。
尽管国会一次性注资 750 亿美元，但 ICE 仍然严重依赖当地警方来寻找将被驱逐出境的人并将其移交。为此，它签署了约 2,600 份协议（其中许多在德克萨斯州），授权当地警察以及其他州和地方机构执行移民法。德克萨斯州一直是 ICE 逮捕的主要目标。
德克萨斯州州长格雷格·阿博特已与特朗普政府密切合作，合作执行联邦移民法。他在第四个任期的竞选中输给了民主党人吉娜·伊诺霍萨。
休斯敦的移民权利组织菲尔一直与帕拉·埃尔南德斯的家人合作，鉴于这一消息，计划于周五下午举行新闻发布会。
Fiel Houston 执行董事塞萨尔·埃斯皮诺萨 (Cesar Espinosa) 表示：“今天休斯顿获胜。休斯顿市议会几个月前就已经做出了决定。”他补充说，是时候贯彻执行了。

title_en: Lawyers descend on Mississippi as vote counting continues in razor-thin Senate race
title_zh: 参议员竞选中计票工作继续进行，律师们纷纷涌入密西西比州
summary: Democratic and Republican lawyers and groups trade sharp legal letters about procedures for counting ballots in tight race Where Trump and Republicans lost the midterms – a visual analysis of the key states Democrat Scott Colom is on the verge of winning a Sen
summary_zh: 民主党和共和党的律师和团体就特朗普和共和党在激烈的竞选中计票程序交换了尖锐的法律信件
body_en: Democratic and Republican lawyers and groups trade sharp legal letters about procedures for counting ballots in tight race
Where Trump and Republicans lost the midterms – a visual analysis of the key states

Democrat Scott Colom is on the verge of winning a Senate seat in Mississippi in a stunning upset, but ballots are still being counted in a close race where Colom holds a lead of just under 2,000 votes over Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith. Losing ruby-red Mississippi would be the final straw for Republicans after a midterm sweep by Democrats that turned Texas blue and saw a Democrat elected to the seat once held by the late South Carolina Republican senator Lindsey Graham.

A possible legal fight is also brewing, as both sides trade sharp legal letters about the procedures for counting remaining ballots. National voting groups and attorneys have descended upon the magnolia state, joining the local groups that worked to mobilize voters. Democratic and Republican groups, including Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee (DSCC) and Democratic election attorneys from the Elias Law Group, have deployed hundreds of volunteers and lawyers to all the state’s 82 counties to oversee the final rounds of counting.
body_zh: 民主党和共和党的律师和团体就激烈竞选中的计票程序交换尖锐的法律信件
特朗普和共和党在中期选举中失败的地方——关键州的可视化分析

民主党人斯科特·科洛姆(Scott Colom)即将以令人震惊的方式赢得密西西比州参议院席位，但在一场势均力敌的竞选中，选票仍在计票中，科洛姆以略低于2,000票的优势领先共和党现任参议员辛迪·海德·史密斯(Cindy Hyde-Smith)。失去红宝石色的密西西比州将成为压垮共和党的最后一根稻草，此前民主党在中期选举中大获全胜，德克萨斯州变成了蓝色，民主党人当选了曾经由已故南卡罗来纳州共和党参议员林赛·格雷厄姆占据的席位。
一场可能的法律斗争也在酝酿之中，双方就剩余选票的清点程序交换了尖锐的法律信件。全国投票团体和律师纷纷来到木兰州，加入努力动员选民的当地团体。民主党和共和党团体，包括民主党参议员竞选委员会 (DSCC) 和来自 Elias Law Group 的民主党选举律师，已向该州所有 82 个县部署了数百名志愿者和律师，以监督最后几轮计票。

title_en: Two more DoJ officials resign, including US attorney leading inquiry into Trump rivals
title_zh: 司法部又有两名官员辞职，其中包括领导对特朗普竞争对手调查的美国检察官
summary: Jason Reding Quiñones led investigation into whether Trump’s rights were violated during 2020 election inquiry A US attorney overseeing the so-called “grand conspiracy” investigation into Donald Trump ’s rivals announced on Friday he is leaving the Department
summary_zh: 杰森·雷丁·奎尼奥内斯 (Jason Reding Quiñones) 领导了一项调查，调查特朗普的权利在 2020 年选举调查期间是否受到侵犯。
body_en: Two more DoJ officials resign, including US attorney leading inquiry into Trump rivals | Trump administration
Jason Reding Quiñones led investigation into whether Trump’s rights were violated during 2020 election inquiry

A US attorney overseeing the so-called “grand conspiracy” investigation into Donald Trump ’s rivals announced on Friday he is leaving the Department of Justice, one of several officials to leave the department in recent days after sweeping Democratic wins in the midterm elections .

Jason Reding Quiñones, the US attorney for the southern district of Florida, and John Eisenberg, who led the justice department’s national security division, are both leaving. Democrats have pledged to use their majorities in the US House and Senate to conduct aggressive oversight of the justice department, among other agencies.

Quiñones had been overseeing an inquiry into whether former top government officials engaged in a “grand conspiracy” to violate Trump’s rights when they investigated him after the 2020 election. Conservative allies had high hopes for the investigation, whose targets included the former CIA director John Brennan, among others.
Harmeet Dhillon, controversial head of DoJ’s civil rights division, steps down

But there were personnel issues and charges have not yet been filed. “The ‘grand conspiracy’ case into the lawfare against the president is essentially dead now,” Julie Kelly, a conservative commentator, posted on X .

“We are grateful for Jason’s leadership in combating violent crime, drug trafficking, sex trafficking and transnational crime, including the indictment of Raúl Castro,” the US attorney general, Todd Blanche, said in a statement.

Eisenberg led the national security division, which oversees terrorism and espionage cases, among others. Eisenberg had previously served in the first Trump administration and has been a top lawyer for the national security council. “He has served with distinction, strengthening our nation’s ability to address threats, both foreign and domestic,” Blanche said in a post on X.

Harmeet Dhillon, the controversial head of the justice department’s civil rights division, also announced she was leaving on Thursday. Dhillon had sought to leave before the midterms and was asked by the White House chief of staff, Susie Wiles, to stay on until after election day.

CBS News reported on Thursday that Trump sought to dismiss Dhillon after her October appearance on 60 Minutes for not more forcefully defending efforts to prosecute non-citizens and send monitors to the polls.

Dhillon told the Guardian she submitted her resignation letter on 13 October, before the 60 Minutes interview aired, and that Wiles asked her to stay on until at least early November. She had also indicated to reporters in August she intended to return to private practice when she left the justice department, according to Bloomberg.
body_zh: 司法部又有两名官员辞职，其中包括领导对特朗普竞争对手调查的美国检察官特朗普政府
Jason Reding Quiñones 领导了关于 2020 年选举调查期间特朗普权利是否受到侵犯的调查
一名负责监督针对唐纳德·特朗普竞争对手的所谓“大阴谋”调查的美国检察官周五宣布，他将离开司法部，这是民主党在中期选举中大获全胜后，最近几天离开司法部的几名官员之一。
佛罗里达州南部地区的美国检察官贾森·雷丁·奎诺内斯和司法部国家安全部门负责人约翰·艾森伯格都将离职。民主党承诺利用其在美国众议院和参议院的多数席位对司法部和其他机构进行积极监督。
奎诺内斯在 2020 年大选后对特朗普进行调查时，一直在监督一项调查，调查前政府高级官员是否参与了侵犯特朗普权利的“大阴谋”。保守派盟友对此次调查寄予厚望，调查目标包括前中央情报局局长约翰·布伦南等人。
备受争议的司法部民权部门负责人哈米特·迪隆 (Harmeet Dhillon) 辞职
但存在人事问题，且尚未提出指控。 “针对总统的‘大阴谋’案件现在基本上已经结束了，”保守派评论员朱莉·凯利(Julie Kelly)在X上发帖称。
美国司法部长托德·布兰奇在一份声明中表示：“我们感谢贾森在打击暴力犯罪、贩毒、性交易和跨国犯罪方面发挥的领导作用，包括起诉劳尔·卡斯特罗。”
艾森伯格领导国家安全部门，负责监督恐怖主义和间谍案件等。艾森伯格此前曾在特朗普第一届政府任职，并曾担任国家安全委员会的高级律师。布兰奇在 X 上的一篇帖子中说：“他表现出色，增强了我们国家应对国内外威胁的能力。”
备受争议的司法部民权部门负责人哈米特·迪伦 (Harmeet Dhillon) 也于周四宣布离职。迪隆曾试图在中期选举前离开，白宫办公厅主任苏西·威尔斯要求他留任至选举日之后。
哥伦比亚广播公司新闻周四报道称，迪隆 10 月份出现在《60 分钟》节目中后，特朗普试图解雇她，因为她没有更有力地捍卫起诉非公民和派遣监察员前往投票站的努力。
迪伦告诉《卫报》，她于 10 月 13 日在《60 分钟》采访播出之前提交了辞职信，怀尔斯要求她至少留任到 11 月初。据彭博社报道，她还在八月份向记者表示，她打算在离开司法部后重返私人诊所。

title_en: DOJ dropping suit asking California to set aside alleged noncitizen ballots
title_zh: 司法部撤销要求加州搁置所谓非公民选票的诉讼
summary: The Justice Department moved to dismiss its own lawsuit that sought to stop California from counting roughly 20,000 ballots it alleged went to noncitizens.
summary_zh: 司法部驳回了自己的诉讼，该诉讼试图阻止加州清点据称流向非公民的约 20,000 张选票
body_en: DOJ moves to drop its lawsuit asking California to set aside alleged noncitizen ballots - CBS News

The Justice Department on Friday moved to dismiss its own lawsuit that sought to stop California from counting roughly 20,000 ballots it alleged went to noncitizens until their immigration status could be verified.

The request to dismiss the case comes days after Republicans' significant losses in the midterm elections and about a week before a scheduled hearing where a special master was slated to evaluate the accuracy of the list. California officials have previously said the list is out of date and includes legitimate voters — a sentiment that the federal judge presiding over the case echoed in his blistering order denying the federal government's request.

The case was at the forefront of the Trump administration's effort to assert control over state-run elections across the country, which Mr. Trump has said are rife with illegal voting without providing evidence.

On Monday, on the eve of Election Day, the Supreme Court rejected an emergency appeal from the Justice Department to require California to separate mail ballots received from the approximately 20,000 people it alleged were noncitizens.
The Supreme Court rejected the appeal in a one-line, unsigned order .

The Justice Department remains enmeshed in litigation with immigrant and voting rights groups seeking to limit its use of the list of what it says are suspected noncitizens. Another controversial lawsuit it filed in Alaska at Mr. Trump's direction before the election to block the victory of the Democrat in that state's Senate race was swiftly dismissed by a federal judge. The administration is appealing that ruling but has yet to file a full brief at the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals.

California had processed roughly 9 million ballots as of early Friday, with nearly 5 million still left to be counted, according to state election officials. The motion to dismiss the lawsuit said that, by the time of the upcoming hearing, the state will have already irreparably "commingled the challenged ballots with lawful ones."
"The relief the United States sought and needed is no longer available—rendering voluntary dismissal necessary," the motion said.

Bill Essayli, the top federal prosecutor in Los Angeles, previously argued in court that the lawsuit would be irrelevant after Election Day, because there would be no way to sequester the ones allegedly belonging to noncitizens. The lawsuit was filed in mid-October, when ballots had been sent to all of the state's 23 million registered voters, and after hundreds of thousands of ballots were already processed. Once a ballot is processed, it is completely anonymized.
Essayli said at the time the lawsuit was filed that his goal was to "safeguard the integrity of the election so it doesn't have an effect on the upcoming election."
"We want to stop the illegal voting. We don't want to chase it later," he said outside of court the week before the election.

The United States Attorney's Office for the Central District of California referred all questions to the Department of Justice in Washington, D.C., which did not respond to an emailed request for comment on Friday evening.

California prosecutors in recent weeks have arrested over 30 noncitizens who are accused of illegally registering to vote. Some who were arrested were also accused of voting in previous elections. Elections clerks around California in the week before the election were sent subpoenas to testify before grand juries slated to convene in November. It's not clear who is being criminally charged in those cases, but the department does not typically subpoena people whom it regards as targets of a criminal investigation to appear before a grand jury.

U.S. District Judge David O. Carter appointed the special master in late October, shortly after allowing California to proceed with elections as planned. Carter, who was appointed by former President Bill Clinton, argued in his blistering order that separating ballots at that late stage would risk disenfranchising citizens and warned it would "wreak havoc" on the midterm elections.
The special master would have also considered whether or not California election officials did in fact have a mechanism for separating the ballots.

司法部周五驳回了自己的诉讼，该诉讼试图阻止加州清点据称发给非公民的大约 20,000 张选票，直到他们的移民身份得到核实。
驳回此案的请求是在共和党在中期选举中惨败的几天后提出的，距离预定的听证会还有一周左右，届时将有一位特别负责人来评估该名单的准确性。加州官员此前曾表示，这份名单已经过时，其中包括合法选民——主审此案的联邦法官在拒绝联邦政府请求的严厉命令中也表达了同样的观点。
此案是特朗普政府试图控制全国范围内的国营选举的最前沿案件，特朗普在没有提供证据的情况下表示，选举中充斥着非法投票。
周一，选举日前夕，最高法院驳回了司法部的紧急上诉，要求加州将收到的大约 20,000 名非公民的邮寄选票分开。
最高法院在一份未签署的单行命令中驳回了上诉。
司法部仍在与移民和投票权团体提起诉讼，寻求限制其使用所谓的疑似非公民名单。大选前，该公司按照特朗普的指示在阿拉斯加州提起了另一起有争议的诉讼，旨在阻止民主党在该州参议员竞选中获胜，但很快就被一名联邦法官驳回。政府正在对该裁决提出上诉，但尚未向第九巡回上诉法院提交完整的案情摘要。
据州选举官员称，截至周五早些时候，加州已处理了约 900 万张选票，仍有近 500 万张选票有待统计。驳回诉讼的动议称，到即将举行的听证会时，该州将已经不可挽回地“将受质疑的选票与合法选票混合在一起”。
动议称：“美国寻求和需要的救济已不再可用，因此有必要自愿解雇。”
洛杉矶最高联邦检察官比尔·埃萨利 (Bill Essayli) 此前在法庭上辩称，选举日之后诉讼将变得无关紧要，因为没有办法扣押据称属于非公民的物品。该诉讼于 10 月中旬提起，当时选票已发送给该州所有 2300 万登记选民，并且数十万张选票已经得到处理。一旦选票被处理，它就会完全匿名。
埃萨利在提起诉讼时表示，他的目标是“维护选举的完整性，以免对即将到来的选举产生影响”。
“我们希望制止非法投票。我们不想稍后再追究，”选举前一周他在法庭外说道。
加州中区联邦检察官办公室将所有问题转交给华盛顿特区司法部，但该部周五晚间没有回复通过电子邮件发送的置评请求。
最近几周，加州检察官逮捕了 30 多名被指控非法登记投票的非公民。一些被捕者还被指控在之前的选举中投票。选举前一周，加州各地的选举工作人员收到传票，要求他们在定于 11 月召开的大陪审团前作证。目前尚不清楚这些案件中谁受到刑事指控，但该部门通常不会传唤其认为是刑事调查目标的人出庭接受大陪审团的审讯。
美国地区法官戴维·卡特 (David O. Carter) 在允许加州按计划进行选举后不久，于 10 月下旬任命了特别法官。由前总统比尔·克林顿任命的卡特在他的严厉命令中辩称，在最后阶段分开选票可能会剥夺公民的选举权，并警告称这将对中期选举“造成严重破坏”。
特别负责人还会考虑加州选举官员是否确实有分离选票的机制。

title_en: What Stephen Miller has pushed for while in Trump administration
title_zh: 斯蒂芬·米勒在特朗普政府期间所推动的目标
summary: Top Trump adviser Stephen Miller, who is set to take over the White House chief of staff role on Monday, has driven President Trump's most controversial immigration policies during both of his administrations.
summary_zh: 特朗普高级顾问斯蒂芬·米勒将于周一接任白宫幕僚长一职，他推动了特朗普总统最具争议性的决策。
body_en: Stephen Miller, Trump's new chief of staff, is the architect of his controversial immigration policies - CBS News

Washington — Top Trump adviser Stephen Miller , who is set to take over the White House chief of staff role on Monday, has driven President Trump's most controversial immigration policies during both of his administrations.
Mr. Trump announced the staffing shake-up on Friday, calling Miller one of his "most trusted" advisers. Miller replaces Susie Wiles, who has been his chief of staff throughout his second term.

The move comes after Republicans suffered crippling losses in the midterm elections and as Democrats plan sweeping investigations into the administration's actions, including its immigration enforcement policies.

Miller was the architect behind many of those policies and also championed the administration's immigration enforcement expansion, which has been supported by approximately $170 billion that congressional Republicans allocated for immigration enforcement and border security in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which became law in July 2025.

During Mr. Trump's first term, Miller helped develop and publicly defend the administration's executive order that restricted entry by nationals of several Muslim-majority countries. The travel ban led to protests around the U.S. and legal challenges. A third iteration of the ban was upheld by the Supreme Court in 2018.

He was a leading supporter of the administration's 2018 zero-tolerance immigration policy, which resulted in thousands of family separations, and he pressed for dramatic reductions in refugee admissions. The administration repeatedly lowered the annual refugee admissions ceiling, ultimately setting it at 15,000 for fiscal year 2021, a record low at the time.
Miller also advocated penalizing legal immigrants who received public benefits and making it harder for them to obtain citizenship.

In Mr. Trump's second term, Miller pushed Immigration and Customs Enforcement to make at least 3,000 immigration arrests per day. In May 2025, Miller publicly demanded a dramatic increase in daily arrests, placing pressure on ICE leadership and expanding enforcement beyond immigrants who had been convicted of serious crimes.
He also proposed that the National Guard be deployed to support mass deportations.

Miller's arrest targets were part of a sweeping expansion of enforcement in communities, workplaces and immigration courts. Detentions of immigrants without criminal histories rose sharply , and increased ICE activity sparked protests across the country.

The longtime Trump adviser also championed the use of a wartime law — the Alien Enemies Act of 1798 — to bypass due process and quickly deport alleged Venezuelan gang members to El Salvador, where they were held in a notorious maximum-security prison, known as CECOT. The deportations set off a legal battle, and the Supreme Court blocked the government from immediately deporting the Venezuelans without giving them an opportunity to challenge their removal.

As part of the administration's deportation efforts, Miller has supported an aggressive expansion of third-country deportations . The administration has deported immigrants to countries where they have no citizenship or family ties, including several African nations .
In May 2025, Miller said the administration was actively considering suspending the constitutional mechanism that allows detainees to challenge their confinement in court.
At a March 2026 conference in Miami, Miller argued that military force, rather than traditional criminal law enforcement alone, was needed to defeat cartels.

Miller appeared alongside Mr. Trump in the Oval Office this summer as he signed executive orders to refuse citizenship to some children born in the United States, after the Supreme Court struck down his earlier executive order aiming to end birthright citizenship.

华盛顿——特朗普高级顾问史蒂芬·米勒(Stephen Miller)将于周一接任白宫幕僚长一职，他在特朗普总统两届政府期间推动了最具争议的移民政策。
特朗普周五宣布了人员调整，称米勒是他“最值得信赖”的顾问之一。米勒接替了苏西·威尔斯，后者在第二个任期内一直担任他的幕僚长。
此举是在共和党在中期选举中遭受惨重损失以及民主党计划对政府行为（包括其移民执法政策）进行全面调查之后做出的。
米勒是其中许多政策背后的设计者，还支持政府扩大移民执法范围，国会共和党人在《美丽大法案》中为移民执法和边境安全拨款约 1,700 亿美元，该法案于 2025 年 7 月成为法律。
在特朗普的第一个任期内，米勒帮助制定并公开捍卫政府限制几个穆斯林占多数国家国民入境的行政命令。旅行禁令引发了美国各地的抗议和法律挑战。 2018 年，最高法院第三次维持该禁令。
他是政府 2018 年零容忍移民政策的主要支持者，该政策导致数千人家庭离散，他敦促大幅减少难民入境人数。政府多次降低年度难民接纳上限，最终将2021财年的难民接纳上限定为15,000人，创下当时的历史新低。
米勒还主张惩罚那些享受公共福利的合法移民，让他们更难获得公民身份。
在特朗普的第二个任期内，米勒推动移民和海关执法局每天逮捕至少 3,000 名移民。 2025 年 5 月，米勒公开要求大幅增加每日逮捕人数，向 ICE 领导层施加压力，并将执法范围扩大到被判犯有严重罪行的移民之外。
他还建议部署国民警卫队来支持大规模驱逐出境。
米勒的逮捕目标是社区、工作场所和移民法庭全面扩大执法力度的一部分。对无犯罪记录的移民的拘留急剧增加，ICE 活动的增加引发了全国各地的抗议活动。
这位特朗普的长期顾问还支持使用战时法律——1798年的《外侨敌人法》——绕过正当程序，迅速将被指控的委内瑞拉帮派成员驱逐到萨尔瓦多，他们被关押在臭名昭著的高度安全监狱，称为CECOT。驱逐引发了一场法律战，最高法院阻止政府立即驱逐委内瑞拉人，而不给他们机会对驱逐提出质疑。
作为政府驱逐出境努力的一部分，米勒支持积极扩大第三国驱逐出境的范围。政府已将移民驱逐到没有公民身份或家庭关系的国家，其中包括几个非洲国家。
2025 年 5 月，米勒表示，政府正在积极考虑暂停允许被拘留者在法庭上质疑其监禁的宪法机制。
在 2026 年 3 月于迈阿密举行的一次会议上，米勒认为，要击败卡特尔，需要军事力量，而不仅仅是传统的刑事执法。
今年夏天，米勒与特朗普一起出现在椭圆形办公室，当时他签署了拒绝给予一些在美国出生的儿童公民身份的行政命令，此前最高法院驳回了他先前旨在终止出生公民权的行政命令。

title_en: Pope voted in U.S. election because he's "proud to be an American"
title_zh: 教皇在美国大选中投票，因为他“为自己是美国人而自豪”
summary: Pope Leo, who is on a 12-day, three-country trip in Latin America, also said he credits God and doctors for his lung cancer surgery recovery.
summary_zh: 教皇利奥正在拉丁美洲三个国家进行为期 12 天的旅行，他还表示，他的肺癌手术康复归功于上帝和医生。
body_en: Pope Leo says he voted in U.S. election because he's "proud to be an American" - CBS News
Pope Leo XIV , who became the first sitting pontiff to vote in a U.S. election , said Friday he is "proud to be an American and to exercise my right" to vote.

His remarks, made to reporters en route to Latin America for a 12-day trip , come after the Vatican confirmed the U.S.-born pontiff had voted via mail-in ballot in his native Chicago. He declined to comment on the outcome of the midterm elections , which gave control of Congress to the Democrats in a repudiation of President Trump. Instead, he pointed to the statement released by the Vatican last week that cited his longstanding belief in civic participation.
The pope, formerly Cardinal Robert Prevost , "has exercised his right to vote as a United States citizen, whenever he was eligible to do so," the Holy See press office said in an Oct. 30 statement.
"The Holy Father expresses his belief in the right and the duty of citizens to participate in democratic processes," the Vatican said in a statement.

The pope has a long history of civic engagement in the U.S., the Vatican said, confirming that during his nearly two decades as a missionary and then bishop in Peru, Leo voted whenever he was eligible. He holds U.S. and Peruvian citizenship.
The Associated Press reported Leo, as Robert Prevost, previously voted in five primary elections since 2000 — on the Democratic ballots in 2008 and 2019 and Republican ballots in 2012, 2014 and 2016.
Leo said Friday that he hadn't been able to vote in Peru's recent election since absentee ballots "aren't possible."
"But I would have done it. It's a good thing," he said, according to the AP.
U.S. federal law allows American citizens, even those who work for foreign governments, to retain their citizenship.

The 71-year-old pope is on a three-nation, 12-day tour just three weeks after he underwent surgery to remove a cancerous tumor from his right lung. He was cleared to travel on Oct. 26 — two weeks after his surgery.

"I am very happy to be here myself. I know some people were doubtful about this trip taking place," Leo told reporters when he greeted them in the back of the plane. "I confess that from the first day, I had no doubt. I was convinced that this trip had to go forward and very happy to say, praise the Lord and thanks to wonderful medical assistance, I am here today, I think, in fairly good shape."
He acknowledged, though, that he hadn't had a chance to play tennis yet.

On Oct. 13, doctors removed the lower lobe of Leo's right lung after discovering a malignant tumor. The cancer, identified as a lung adenocarcinoma, was discovered accidentally during a routine abdominal examination, his doctors said. The operation was successful, without complications , and Leo was discharged from the hospital on Oct. 17.

"Early detection is obviously the best way to go, and so regular checkups are a blessing," Leo said, crediting his recovery to "trusting God, good doctors, good surgeons, and overall I think a healthy lifestyle."
The Associated Press contributed to this report.

body_zh: 教皇利奥表示，他在美国大选中投票是因为他“为自己是美国人而感到自豪” - 哥伦比亚广播公司新闻
教皇利奥十四世成为第一位在美国大选中投票的现任教皇，他周五表示，他“为自己是一名美国人并行使自己的投票权感到自豪”。
他在前往拉丁美洲进行为期 12 天的访问途中对记者发表上述言论之前，梵蒂冈证实这位出生于美国的教皇已在其家乡芝加哥通过邮寄选票进行了投票。他拒绝对中期选举的结果发表评论，中期选举将国会控制权交给了民主党，从而否定了特朗普总统。相反，他指出梵蒂冈上周发布的声明，其中引用了他长期以来对公民参与的信念。
罗马教廷新闻办公室在 10 月 30 日的一份声明中表示，前红衣主教罗伯特·普雷沃斯特的教皇“只要有资格，就以美国公民的身份行使了投票权”。
梵蒂冈在一份声明中表示：“教宗表达了他对公民参与民主进程的权利和义务的信念。”
梵蒂冈表示，教皇在美国有着悠久的公民参与历史，并证实，在他担任秘鲁传教士和主教的近二十年里，利奥只要有资格就会投票。他拥有美国和秘鲁公民身份。
据美联社报道，利奥（化名罗伯特·普雷沃斯特）自 2000 年以来曾参加过五次初选，其中包括 2008 年和 2019 年的民主党选票以及 2012 年、2014 年和 2016 年的共和党选票。
利奥周五表示，他无法在秘鲁最近的选举中投票，因为缺席投票“不可能”。
据美联社报道，他说：“但我会这么做。这是一件好事。”
美国联邦法律允许美国公民，甚至是为外国政府工作的人，保留其公民身份。
这位 71 岁的教皇在接受右肺癌肿瘤切除手术后仅三周，就开始了为期 12 天的三个国家的访问。 10 月 26 日，即手术两周后，他获准出行。
“我很高兴自己来到这里。我知道有些人对这次旅行持怀疑态度，”利奥在飞机后部迎接他们时告诉记者。 “我承认，从第一天起，我就毫无疑问。我确信这次旅行必须继续进行，并且很高兴地说，赞美主，感谢出色的医疗援助，我认为今天我的状态相当好。”
不过，他承认他还没有机会打网球。
10月13日，医生在发现利奥的右肺下叶患有恶性肿瘤后，切除了他的右肺下叶。他的医生说，这种癌症被确定为肺腺癌，是在例行腹部检查时意外发现的。手术很成功，没有出现并发症，Leo于10月17日出院。
利奥说：“早期发现显然是最好的方法，因此定期检查是一种祝福。”他将自己的康复归功于“相信上帝、好医生、好外科医生，以及总体而言我认为健康的生活方式。”
美联社对此报道作出了贡献。

body_en: Up First briefing: Jobs report; Trump's arch; Public schools; Dhillon : NPR

Up First briefing: Jobs report; Trump's arch; Public schools; Dhillon A judge has blocked construction of Trump's arch moments after it won federal approval to proceed. And, the Labor Department is set to release the latest jobs report today, a day after stocks plunged.
Your support helps make our show possible and unlocks access to our sponsor-free feed.
Post-Election Market & Jobs, Why Gas Prices Could Stay High, Trump's Arch Blocked

Rising prices and stagnant wages fueled frustration during this week's midterm elections , prompting voters to express their discontent at the ballot box. Similarly, the stock market experienced a downturn yesterday. Concerns about a Democratic Congress regulating AI led to a more than 5% drop in the tech-heavy Nasdaq , wiping out more than $2 trillion in market value. This decline followed from Wednesday when shares rose as investors were relieved that the midterms had made Congress's fate clear. In contrast, there has been less volatility in the job market, and today the Labor Department is set to release the latest jobs report.

Stocks sank as investors fear an incoming Democratic Congress — and states across the country — could crack down on the AI industry and data centers. TIMOTHY A. CLARY/AFP via Getty Images/AFP hide caption

🎧 Today's jobs report is expected to show that employers added about 60,000 jobs last month, NPR's Scott Horsley tells Up First . While this isn't robust growth, it should keep the unemployment rate low . As long as the job market stays stable, the Federal Reserve can focus on fighting stubbornly high inflation, which likely drove the recent election outcomes.

A federal judge has temporarily blocked construction of President Trump's 250-foot arch in the capital. District Court Judge Tanya Chutkan issued an order just before midnight Friday, halting work for 14 day s at the request of D.C. and Virginia governments. In her 33-page opinion, she scrutinized the administration's justifications for the arch, particularly its focus on national security and agreed that the local governments are likely to be harmed by its construction. The arch is planned for Memorial Circle, a traffic island on the bridge linking the Lincoln Memorial to Arlington National Cemetery.

🎧 The judges' decision followed a contentious meeting last night , during which the National Capital Planning Commission, filled with Trump allies, voted to approve the arch, NPR's Rachel Treisman says. The commission's approval came despite significant opposition to the arch from dozens and dozens of people. After nearly nine hours, the panel gave the go-ahead, which would have allowed excavation to begin. Several Democratic lawmakers are already talking about blocking the arch. Democrat Jared Huffman of California, likely to become head of the House Natural Resources Committee, warned commissioners at yesterday's meeting that anyone advancing projects not authorized by Congress risks legal repercussions.

School enrollment is set to plunge by another 2 million kids by 2030 , and education experts say the crisis will be worsened by the deportation of immigrant families with school-age children. Even before the Trump administration's policy changes, public schools faced a significant decline due to shrinking family sizes. U.S. Census data show the number of children under 18 nationwide had fallen by about 2.1 million since 2010. The Trump administration's large-scale deportations began after public schools started facing a demographic crisis, with a Migration Policy Institute study indicating that 1.9 million people left the U.S. during Trump's second term. This situation marks the first time in nearly a century that birth rates and immigration levels are both low at the same time .

Harmeet Dhillon has left her position as head of the Justice Department's Civil Rights Division after 18 tumultuous months. During her time in the role, she transformed the unit, saw a significant loss of career staff and aggressively pursued Trump's agenda. She is the first senior official to depart since Democrats gained control of Congress in the midterms. Dhillon called the role "the honor of a lifetime."
Father and son holding toothbrushes and toothpaste in a bathroom, sharing a relaxed morning oral care routine together. mihailomilovanovic/Getty Images hide caption
Healthy or Hype? is an NPR series helping readers and listeners sort truth from fiction when it comes to online health claims.

Many people are replacing their fluoride dental products with those containing hydroxyapatite. It is a mineral that boasts cavity protection, whitening and enamel strengthening — all without fluoride. While health experts widely agree that fluoride is beneficial to health, interest in fluoride-free alternatives is growing. A driving force behind the trend is Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. blaming water fluoridation for health issues like arthritis, bone fractures, bone cancer and neurodevelopmental disorders. Here's what dentists say about it .
🪥 Fluoride has been extensively researched, especially in long-term studies, but early research on hydroxyapatite shows promising results.

🪥 For patients considering both options, Bennett Amaechi, a professor of dentistry at the University of Texas at San Antonio, recommends using fluoride because there is more evidence supporting its effectiveness.

🪥 Amaechi was an author of a 2021 study in Scientific Reports that followed 177 children for a year and compared hydroxyapatite and fluoride toothpaste. The findings showed similar outcomes of tooth decay in both groups.

🪥 The American Dental Association told NPR that it acknowledges that more people are using hydroxyapatite products, which may aid in remineralization. However, they noted that research on its clinical effectiveness is still limited and unclear.
🪥 The ADA recommends brushing teeth twice daily for two minutes with fluoride toothpaste, flossing every day and visiting a dentist regularly.

NPR 的雷切尔·特雷斯曼 (Rachel Treisman) 表示，法官们的决定是在昨晚一场有争议的会议之后做出的，会议期间，由特朗普盟友组成的国家首都规划委员会投票批准了这座拱门。尽管数十人强烈反对这座拱门，委员会还是批准了。近九个小时后，专家组批准了挖掘工作，开始了挖掘工作。一些民主党议员已经在讨论封锁拱门的问题。可能成为众议院自然资源委员会主席的加利福尼亚州民主党人贾里德·霍夫曼在昨天的会议上警告委员们，任何推进未经国会授权的项目的人都可能面临法律后果。

到 2030 年，入学人数预计将再减少 200 万，教育专家表示，有学龄儿童的移民家庭被驱逐出境将使危机进一步恶化。甚至在特朗普政府改变政策之前，公立学校就因家庭规模缩小而面临大幅下降。美国人口普查数据显示，自 2010 年以来，全国 18 岁以下儿童数量减少了约 210 万。在公立学校开始面临人口危机后，特朗普政府开始大规模驱逐出境，移民政策研究所的一项研究表明，在特朗普第二任期内，有 190 万人离开美国。这种情况标志着近一个世纪以来首次出现出生率和移民水平同时较低的情况。
在经历了 18 个月的动荡之后，哈米特·迪伦 (Harmeet Dhillon) 辞去了司法部民权司司长的职务。在任职期间，她对部门进行了改造，看到职业员工大量流失，并积极推行特朗普的议程。她是自民主党在中期选举中控制国会以来第一位离职的高级官员。迪伦称这个角色是“一生的荣幸”。

健康还是炒作？是 NPR 的一个系列节目，帮助读者和听众在网上健康声明方面辨别真假。
许多人正在用含有羟基磷灰石的产品取代含氟牙科产品。它是一种具有蛀牙保护、美白和强化牙釉质功效的矿物质，而且不含氟化物。虽然健康专家普遍认为氟化物有益于健康，但人们对无氟化物替代品的兴趣正在与日俱增。这一趋势背后的推动力是卫生部长小罗伯特·肯尼迪 (Robert F. Kennedy Jr.)，他将关节炎、骨折、骨癌和神经发育障碍等健康问题归咎于水氟化。以下是牙医对此的评价。
🪥 氟化物已被广泛研究，特别是在长期研究中，但对羟基磷灰石的早期研究显示出有希望的结果。
🪥 对于考虑这两种选择的患者，德克萨斯大学圣安东尼奥分校的牙科教授 Bennett Amaechi 建议使用氟化物，因为有更多证据支持其有效性。
🪥 Amaechi 是《科学报告》2021 年一项研究的作者，该研究跟踪了 177 名儿童一年，并对羟基磷灰石和氟化物牙膏进行了比较。研究结果显示，两组的蛀牙结果相似。
🪥 美国牙科协会告诉 NPR，它承认越来越多的人正在使用羟基磷灰石产品，这可能有助于再矿化。然而，他们指出，对其临床有效性的研究仍然有限且不清楚。
🪥 ADA 建议每天使用含氟牙膏刷牙两次，每次两分钟，每天使用牙线并定期看牙医。

body_en: Jeffries lays out Democrats' plans for Congress, questions remain about accountability : NPR

Jeffries lays out Democrats' plans for Congress, questions remain about accountability Speaking with Morning Edition , Hakeem Jeffries discussed ending the Iran war, holding Trump accountable and calls for new Democratic leadership, but offered few specifics on how Democrats would deliver.
Democrats ran on affordability. What's the party's plan?
Back in the majority, Democrats have plans for a long list of Trump investigations

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, the New York Democrat who is poised to become the next Speaker of the House , says his party will push to end the war in Iran and hold Trump administration officials accountable after its midterm victories. But how far Democrats will go remains unclear.
Despite the hardships of war, Iran's rulers still have a base of support
Speaking with Morning Edition on Friday, Jeffries called the conflict a "war of choice" that "has skyrocketed gas prices, diesel prices and fertilizer prices," raising the cost of everyday goods.
He said Democrats "shouldn't have to wait" for the new Congress to act.

But with majorities in both chambers, Jeffries said Democrats could pass a war powers resolution to try and force President Trump to end the war. If passed, it would present President Trump with the choice to either sign or veto it. Overriding a veto would require two-thirds majorities in both chambers. As of now, Democrats are short of a veto-proof majority in both chambers.
Three ways Democrats could reshape U.S. foreign policy after the midterms
Jeffries stopped short of supporting impeachment proceedings against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.
Republican Rep. Thomas Massie of Kentucky has threatened to force a House vote on eight articles of impeachment unless Hegseth resigns.
"We'll have that conversation," Jeffries said, calling Hegseth "the most unqualified secretary of defense in American history."
Asked directly whether Hegseth should be impeached, Jeffries said, "I don't want to get out ahead of the caucus."
Jeffries said the House Judiciary and Oversight committees would investigate alleged wrongdoing by the Trump administration.

Asked about voters calling for new Democratic leadership, including the next House speaker, Jeffries said the decision rests with the House Democratic Caucus. He defended Democrats' record, saying they had "battled Trump on every issue up until this point and then just decisively defeated him a few days ago."
Listen to the full interview using the blue button above, or read the transcript below, lightly edited for length and clarity.

Leila Fadel: The person expected to be the next House Speaker and its first Black Speaker is the current House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, and he joins me now to talk about what that will look like. So your party has a real mandate here in Congress, and it comes with expectations from voters that you'll make life more affordable. What is at the top of your agenda if you're elected House Speaker?

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries: Well, it was a tremendous victory for the American people and a strong rebuke of MAGA extremism, which has made life more expensive for everyday Americans. Despite their promises to lower the high cost of living on day one. There are several steps that we can take to create a more comfortable way of life for the American people, including ending the war of choice in Iran, which has skyrocketed gas prices, diesel prices, and fertilizer prices, and as a result, increased the cost of groceries and everyday goods on the American people.

杰弗里斯周五在接受早间版采访时称，这场冲突是一场“选择之战”，“导致汽油价格、柴油价格和化肥价格飙升”，提高了日常用品的成本。
他表示，民主党人“不必等待”新国会采取行动。
但杰弗里斯表示，凭借参众两院的多数席位，民主党可以通过一项战争权力决议，试图迫使特朗普总统结束战争。如果获得通过，特朗普总统将可以选择签署或否决该法案。推翻否决权需要参众两院均获得三分之二多数票。截至目前，民主党在参众两院均缺乏可否决的多数席位。
中期选举后民主党重塑美国外交政策的三种方式
杰弗里斯没有支持针对国防部长皮特·赫格斯的弹劾程序。
肯塔基州共和党众议员托马斯·马西威胁称，除非赫格斯辞职，否则将迫使众议院就八项弹劾条款进行投票。
杰弗里斯说：“我们将会进行这样的对话。”他称赫格斯是“美国历史上最不合格的国防部长”。
当被直接问及是否应该弹劾赫格斯时，杰弗里斯说：“我不想在党团会议之前退出。”
杰弗里斯表示，众议院司法和监督委员会将调查特朗普政府涉嫌的不当行为。
