title_zh: 布鲁克斯和卡普哈特谈特朗普的白宫改组和中期选举的影响
summary: David Brooks of The Atlantic and Jonathan Capehart of MS NOW join Geoff Bennett to discuss the week in politics, including Trump shaking up his White House leadership, deep divisions in the Republican Party and how Democrats are preparing to take control of Co
summary_zh: 《大西洋月刊》的大卫·布鲁克斯和《MS NOW》的乔纳森·卡普哈特与杰夫·贝内特一起讨论本周的政治，包括特朗普撼动他的白宫
body_en: https://www.pbs.org/newshour/show/brooks-and-capehart-on-trumps-white-house-shakeup-and-fallout-from-the-midterms

David Brooks of The Atlantic and Jonathan Capehart of MS NOW join Geoff Bennett to discuss the week in politics, including Trump shaking up his White House leadership, deep divisions in the Republican Party and how Democrats are preparing to take control of Congress.
Notice: Transcripts are machine and human generated and lightly edited for accuracy. They may contain errors.
Well, President Trump is shaking up his White House leadership, Republicans are confronting deep divisions within their party, and Democrats are preparing to take control of Congress.
For more on what comes next, we turn to Brooks and Capehart. That's David Brooks of "The Atlantic" and Jonathan Capehart of MS NOW.

And we end it with President Trump announcing that Stephen Miller will replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff. After one of the most devastating midterm defeats in modern history, the president is elevating one of the architects of his most hard-line policy.
David, your reaction. How's it all strike you?

Stunning. Stunning. He's going for the wartime consigliere, which is what Stephen Miller is. I guess they're going to the mattresses, as they would say. I spent a week in Sicily, so I got a lot of "Godfather" references.

I just think he's going with the guy who's the ultimate loyalist. And he's I think sending Susie Wiles over to help pick the nominee for the next Republican, on the illusion that he has going to have much of a say in who's the next nominee.

I have really been struck by how so many Republicans are unleashed, not all in public. The one who's been most public is Ron DeSantis, the Florida governor. After the election, he was unleashed, and he was just furious about what's happened to the party, how it's been destroyed. He called this election a near-extinction event for the Republican Party.

And a lot of Republicans feel that. A lot of other Republicans, I would say, are just quiet. They have gone sullen. And so how that shakes out, but I don't think there's going to be much flavor for more of the same, which is what Stephen Miller is, doubling down on the same.

Our Liz Landers reports that Susie Wiles submitted her resignation last night. And there's other reporting that President Trump was angry with Wiles after the GOP's shellacking in this week's midterm election.
Is Stephen Miller's elevation, Jonathan, the clearest signal yet that President Trump has no intention of changing course?

I mean, I think, pardon the imagery I'm about to present, Stephen Miller's elevation is a big middle finger to the American voters, what they had to say through their votes on Tuesday, to the incoming Democratic majorities. How are they going to -- it just seems to me this is the clearest indication that the president has even -- has given up even pretending that he wants to govern.

My hope is that -- to pick up on what David was saying about Republicans, is that the behavior of the Republicans who come back to Washington in the 120th Congress, that their behavior will change. And I'm particularly looking at Republican senators.

Lisa Murkowski is going to need some other moderates to join her in working with Democrats to get things done. I mean, Democrats have a lot on their plate, given the results of the election. But so do -- but so do Republicans.

And I would hope that there are some moderates within the Republican Party, because I do know that there are some, will start to assert themselves, especially if they're thinking of running for president themselves in '28.
In order for that to happen, Republicans would have to believe that MAGA is no longer a potent political force. Tucker Carlson said last night on his show that the Trump era is over. Is he right?

For this election, people don't -- in 2010, when Barack Obama suffered that shellacking, he -- the Republicans had an advantage of 7 percentage points up in the total House race. This time, the Democrats had a total House race advantage of 13 points. So it was twice as big as 2010, which we considered this massive midterm setback for the president.
body_zh: 《大西洋月刊》的大卫·布鲁克斯和《MS NOW》的乔纳森·卡普哈特与杰夫·贝内特一起讨论本周的政治，包括特朗普撼动白宫领导层、共和党内部的深刻分歧以及民主党准备如何控制国会。
注意：文字记录由机器和人工生成，并经过轻微编辑以保证准确性。它们可能包含错误。
特朗普总统正在动摇他的白宫领导层，共和党人正面临党内的深刻分歧，而民主党人正准备控制国会。
有关接下来发生的事情的更多信息，我们求助于布鲁克斯和卡普哈特。那是《大西洋月刊》的大卫·布鲁克斯和《MS NOW》的乔纳森·卡普哈特。
最后，特朗普总统宣布斯蒂芬·米勒将接替苏西·威尔斯担任白宫办公厅主任。在经历了现代历史上最具毁灭性的中期选举失败之一后，总统正在提拔他最强硬政策的设计者之一。
大卫，你的反应。这一切让你感觉如何？
令人惊叹的。令人惊叹的。他将担任战时军师，斯蒂芬·米勒就是这样的人。正如他们所说，我猜他们会去床垫。我在西西里待了一周，所以得到了很多《教父》的参考资料。
我只是认为他会和一个最忠诚的人在一起。我认为他会派苏西·威尔斯去帮助挑选下一任共和党的提名人，因为他幻想自己对谁是下一个提名人有很大的发言权。
令我震惊的是，这么多共和党人的言论自由，而不是全部公开。最为公开的是佛罗里达州州长罗恩·德桑蒂斯 (Ron DeSantis)。选举结束后，他被释放了，他对党所发生的事情以及它是如何被摧毁感到愤怒。他称这次选举是共和党濒临灭绝的事件。
很多共和党人都有这种感觉。我想说，很多其他共和党人只是保持沉默。他们变得闷闷不乐。这就是如何产生的，但我认为更多相同的东西不会有太多味道，这就是斯蒂芬·米勒（Stephen Miller）所做的，在相同的东西上加倍努力。
我们的利兹·兰德斯报道说苏西·怀尔斯昨晚提交了辞呈。还有其他报道称，在共和党在本周的中期选举中遭受惨败后，特朗普总统对怀尔斯感到愤怒。
乔纳森，斯蒂芬·米勒的晋升是迄今为止特朗普总统无意改变路线的最明确信号吗？
我的意思是，我想，请原谅我即将呈现的形象，斯蒂芬·米勒的晋升对美国选民来说是一个巨大的中指，他们必须通过周二的投票向即将到来的民主党多数派说的话。他们将如何——在我看来，这是总统最明显的迹象——甚至放弃假装他想执政。
我希望——按照大卫关于共和党人的说法，在第 120 届国会回到华盛顿的共和党人的行为，他们的行为将会改变。我特别关注共和党参议员。
丽莎·默科斯基将需要其他一些温和派人士与她一起与民主党合作以完成工作。我的意思是，考虑到选举结果，民主党有很多事情要做。但共和党人也是如此。
我希望共和党内有一些温和派，因为我确实知道有一些，会开始坚持自己的立场，特别是如果他们考虑在 28 年竞选总统。
为了实现这一目标，共和党人必须相信 MAGA 不再是一支强大的政治力量。塔克·卡尔森昨晚在节目中表示，特朗普时代已经结束。他说得对吗？
对于这次选举，人们不这么认为——2010年，当巴拉克·奥巴马(Barack Obama)遭受惨败时，他——共和党在众议院总选举中领先7个百分点。这次，民主党在众议院竞选中总共领先 13 个百分点。所以它的规模是 2010 年的两倍，我们认为那一年对总统来说是一次巨大的中期挫折。

title_en: Inside the early GOP reckoning after historic defeat
title_zh: 共和党历史性失败后的早期清算
summary: Stephen Miller's rise to chief of staff exacerbated GOP fears that there will be no party-wide reckoning after their midterm wipeout.
summary_zh: 斯蒂芬·米勒 (Stephen Miller) 升任幕僚长加剧了共和党的担忧，即他们在中期选举中惨败后将不会进行全党范围内的清算。
body_en: President Donald Trump's decision to name hard-line loyalist Stephen Miller as his top aide cemented what many Republicans were already privately fearing: There will be no party-wide GOP reckoning with this week's midterm bloodbath.

Instead, with Trump still in office for another two years, most have grown resigned to the reality that the president is going to lean in on a confrontational approach with Congress — and is not willing to change course.

Republicans on Capitol Hill and inside the Trump administration are questioning how and whether they can break with the president now after having green-lit much of his agenda, according to more than a dozen GOP lawmakers, senior aides and Trump officials interviewed for this story, some of whom were granted anonymity to speak candidly about the party’s future.
Trump's decision Friday to elevate Miller, the architect of his unpopular mass deportation policy and an advocate of fierce partisan confrontation, crystallized the frustration.

“There needs to be some self-reflection for Republicans,” Rep. Marlin Stutzman (R-Ind.) said in an interview about the midterm losses Friday morning. “There should be some heads rolling at the White House because we lost badly.”
Hours later, heads did roll. Trump announced Miller would replace Susie Wiles as his new chief of staff.
“Horrible decision,” Stutzman said in response.
One House Republican, when informed that Trump had named Miller his chief of staff, replied: “Please tell me you’re lying to me right now, just to get a reaction.”

The immediate aftermath of the election has sharpened the GOP’s core issue for the past decade: They are struggling to navigate the man who they reshaped their entire identity around, and whose record low approval with voters helped to fuel generational losses within the party.
The Iran war is another area where some Republicans are having regrets. Vice President JD Vance identified it as the main reason for the party’s defeat in his election post-mortem.
The problem with Vance’s assessment, one senior Hill Republican said, is, “we’ve been fucking voting for the war since March — because they told us to.”
Republicans and Trump advisers expect the president to wield massive influence in the 2028 GOP primaries, another reason many are staying quiet.

"Everyone is staring at each other and wondering who will speak up and blame Trump first," said one GOP operative who worked on a battleground race Democrats won. They, like others in this article, were granted anonymity to speak candidly. "But we've been here before. I'm not holding my breath. He still controls the party and its primaries, at least for now."
The White House responded to POLITICO's request for comment by referring to Trump's praise for Miller on Friday. The RNC declined to comment.

Miller wrote on social media that he is "honored beyond words to serve as [Trump's] White House Chief of Staff" and "the mission now is more clear than ever: Fight with all of our soul to support our President."

How much lawmakers will distance themselves will be put to the test quickly: House Republicans will have an immediate opportunity to break with Trump and the war next week, when Rep. Thomas Massie said in an interview with POLITICO he will trigger his articles of impeachment against Secretary Pete Hegseth. “There are a lot of questions about Hegseth,” House Oversight Chair James Comer (R-Ky.) said Friday.

Some senior Republicans are privately nudging Trump officials to ditch Hegseth before the vote, according to two people with direct knowledge of the conversations. The White House is sticking by Hegseth so far, however.

House Republicans will also have a chance to elect new leadership next week, including a new chair of the National Republican Congressional Committee. But in a sign of what’s to come, none of the candidates — including Reps. Brian Jack (R-Ga.) and Rudy Yakym (R-Ind.) — nor any other GOP leadership candidates have publicly suggested doing more to break with Trump.

A small group of Republicans on Capitol Hill have privately declared, as of Tuesday night, that “MAGA is over,” and it’s time for a “reset,” as one House GOP aide put it — and yet it’s a sentiment no prominent Republican is willing to say publicly.

Rep. Chris Smith (R-N.J.), one of the longest-serving members of the House, said he wasn’t going to “blame” others for Tuesday’s losses, which left him as the sole GOP incumbent survivor in his home state. Asked if Republicans were dragged down by the president, Smith replied: “I don’t want to answer that.”
body_zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统决定任命强硬派忠诚者斯蒂芬·米勒为他的高级助手，这加剧了许多共和党人私下里已经担心的事情：共和党将不会对本周的中期选举大屠杀进行清算。
相反，随着特朗普再执政两年，大多数人已经接受了总统将采取与国会对抗的方式的现实，并且不愿意改变路线。
接受采访的十多名共和党议员、高级助手和特朗普官员表示，国会山和特朗普政府内部的共和党人在为总统的大部分议程开绿灯后，正在质疑如何以及是否可以与总统决裂。其中一些人被要求匿名，可以坦率地谈论该党的未来。
特朗普周五决定提拔米勒，他是他不受欢迎的大规模驱逐政策的缔造者，也是激烈党派对抗的倡导者，这让人们的挫败感更加具体化。
“共和党人需要进行一些自我反思，”众议员马林·斯塔茨曼（印第安纳州共和党人）在周五上午接受采访时谈到中期选举的失利时表示。 “白宫应该有一些人在摇头，因为我们输得很惨。”
几个小时后，人们的头开始转动。特朗普宣布米勒将接替苏西·威尔斯担任新任幕僚长。
“可怕的决定，”斯图茨曼回应道。
一位众议院共和党人在得知特朗普任命米勒为幕僚长后回答道：“请告诉我，你现在在对我撒谎，只是为了得到回应。”
选举的直接后果使共和党在过去十年中的核心问题变得更加尖锐：他们正在努力引导这个人重塑他们的整个身份，而他在选民中的支持率创历史新低，加剧了党内的代际损失。
伊朗战争是一些共和党人感到遗憾的另一个领域。副总统万斯认为这是该党在选举失败的主要原因。
一位资深希尔共和党人表示，万斯评估的问题在于，“自三月份以来，我们一直在投票支持战争——因为他们告诉我们这样做。”
共和党人和特朗普顾问预计总统将在 2028 年共和党初选中发挥巨大影响力，这是许多人保持沉默的另一个原因。
“每个人都盯着对方，想知道谁会首先站出来指责特朗普，”一位曾参与民主党获胜的战场竞选的共和党特工表示。和本文中的其他人一样，他们被允许匿名坦诚发言。 “但我们以前来过这里。我没有屏住呼吸。他仍然控制着该党及其初选，至少目前如此。”
白宫在回应《政治》杂志的置评请求时提到了特朗普周五对米勒的赞扬。共和党全国委员会拒绝发表评论。
米勒在社交媒体上写道，他“能够担任（特朗普的）白宫办公厅主任，感到难以言表的荣幸”，“现在的使命比以往任何时候都更加明确：全力以赴支持我们的总统。”
议员们会保持多大的距离将很快受到考验：众议院共和党人下周将有立即机会与特朗普和战争决裂，届时众议员托马斯·马西在接受《政治》杂志采访时表示，他将触发针对国务卿皮特·赫格斯的弹劾条款。 “关于赫格斯的问题有很多，”众议院监督主席詹姆斯·科默（肯塔基州共和党人）周五表示。
据两位直接了解谈话情况的人士透露，一些资深共和党人正在私下敦促特朗普官员在投票前抛弃赫格塞斯。然而，白宫到目前为止仍坚持赫格斯的观点。
众议院共和党人下周还将有机会选举新的领导层，包括全国共和党国会委员会的新主席。但未来的一个迹象是，包括佐治亚州共和党众议员布莱恩·杰克(Brian Jack)和印第安纳州共和党众议员鲁迪·亚基姆(Rudy Yakym)在内的所有候选人，以及任何其他共和党领导候选人都没有公开建议采取更多措施来与特朗普决裂。
截至周二晚间，国会山的一小群共和党人私下宣称，“MAGA 已经结束”，正如一位众议院共和党助手所说，现在是“重置”的时候了，但没有一位知名共和党人愿意公开表达这种情绪。
众议员克里斯·史密斯（R-N.J.）是众议院任职时间最长的议员之一，他表示，他不会将周二的失利“归咎于”其他人，这使他成为家乡唯一的共和党现任幸存者。当被问及共和党人是否被总统拖累时，史密斯回答说：“我不想回答这个问题。”

Thomas Markle, the father of Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex , was arrested by US federal agents in Florida on Friday and charged in connection with possession of child sexual abuse material, according to the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI).

In his first public appearance after an election that soundly repudiated his policies, President Donald Trump turned to a topic both familiar and, given the context, surprising
By GARY FIELDS Associated Press and LISA MASCARO Associated Press

WASHINGTON -- In his first public appearance after an election that soundly repudiated his policies, President Donald Trump turned to a topic both familiar and, given the context, surprising: not his policies or politics, but his efforts to remake pieces of the city that is the backdrop to his presidency.

Despite Trump’s affinity for project management, though, with Democrats taking control of Congress, the work the administration is doing to change the physical face of the District of Columbia is sure to face far more roadblocks than it did for the first two years of his second term.

From the renaming of and renovation plans for the Kennedy Center to remaking a public golf course and erecting an arch 100 feet (30.48 meters) taller than the Statue of Liberty without its pedestal, the president has been deeply involved in how D.C. looks. Democrats have voiced opposition but, in terms of power, have been in the wilderness.

The potential collision point between an oppositional oversight from Democrats and the president's preoccupation with the projects was evident in his last message to the American public before the election — and in his first afterward, too.

Both focused to some degree on his projects. On Monday, it was the reflecting pool in front of the Lincoln Memorial ; on Wednesday, it was a tour of the under-construction White House ballroom, where he talked columns and steel beams and Corinthian designs.

Rep. Jared Huffman of California, the top Democrat on the Natural Resources Committee with jurisdiction over the Interior Department that is involved with operations at parks and federal lands, spent much of the past year probing and questioning Trump’s projects, laying the groundwork for this moment.

“We’ve pushed back against vanity projects that seek to transform treasured public spaces into gaudy tributes to Trump. We exposed corruption, uncovered the efforts to hijack America’s 250th birthday, demanded accountability, and offered a compelling alternative governing vision grounded in science, fairness, environmental responsibility, and the rule of law,” Huffman said in a letter to colleagues seeking their support to be chairman.

As chairman with a strong Democratic majority, “I will ensure that the Committee’s full investigative and oversight authority is leveraged to uncover wrongdoing, demand accountability, and protect the public interest," he said.

Trump has been rushing the various projects, a point Virginia Democratic Rep. Don Beyer made Thursday at a public hearing when he opposed construction of the memorial arch the president has planned in Memorial Circle directly across the Memorial Bridge from the Lincoln Memorial.
"The appropriations process beginning Jan. 3 will be controlled by Democrats. That will be one of the ways Congressman Beyer will step in,” said Beyer’s spokesman Aaron Fritschner.
A less appreciated impact will be the change in who names the general counsel of the House. The House Speaker has that role, presumably Rep. Hakeem Jeffries.

While Democrats have joined in lawsuits opposing the various projects, their filings don't carry the weight of Congress as the minority. “You’ll see the new majority pulling back the balance of power that (House Speaker) Mike Johnson was willing to cede,” Fritschner said.

Beyer has already been a critic, Fritschner said, and cited other members who have signed on in amicus briefs. More than 120 witnesses were on hand for the National Capital Planning Commission meeting, which ran for 9 ½ hours late into Thursday night.

The commission gave the 250-foot (76-meter) arch its final approval on an 8-4 vote, before a federal judge stepped in before midnight to block the Trump administration from breaking ground for 14 days.

加里·菲尔兹美联社和丽莎·马斯卡罗美联社报道
华盛顿——唐纳德·特朗普总统在选举后首次公开露面，彻底否定了他的政策，他转向了一个既熟悉又令人惊讶的话题：不是他的政策或政治，而是他为重塑这座作为其总统任期背景的城市所做的努力。
尽管特朗普热衷于项目管理，但随着民主党控制国会，政府为改变哥伦比亚特区的面貌所做的工作肯定会面临比他第二任期前两年更多的障碍。
从肯尼迪中心的重命名和改造计划，到重建公共高尔夫球场，再到建造一座比没有基座的自由女神像高 100 英尺（30.48 米）的拱门，总统一直深入参与华盛顿特区的面貌。民主党虽然表示反对，但在权力方面却一直处于荒野状态。
民主党的反对派监督与总统对这些项目的全神贯注之间的潜在冲突点在他大选前向美国公众发出的最后一条信息中显而易见，在大选后的第一条信息中也很明显。
两人都在某种程度上专注于他的项目。周一，是林肯纪念堂前的倒影池；周三，他参观了正在建设中的白宫宴会厅，在那里他谈论了柱子、钢梁和科林斯式设计。
加利福尼亚州众议员贾里德·霍夫曼 (Jared Huffman) 是自然资源委员会的最高民主党人，负责管辖内政部，负责公园和联邦土地的运营。去年，他花了大部分时间探索和质疑特朗普的项目，为这一刻奠定了基础。
“我们抵制了那些试图将珍贵的公共空间变成对特朗普的华而不实的致敬的虚荣项目。我们揭露了腐败，揭露了劫持美国250周年生日的行为，要求问责，并提供了一个基于科学、公平、环境责任和法治的令人信服的替代治理愿景，”霍夫曼在一封致寻求支持担任主席的同事的信中表示。
作为拥有强大民主党多数席位的主席，“我将确保充分利用委员会的调查和监督权力来揭露不当行为、要求问责并保护公共利益，”他说。
特朗普一直在加紧推进各种项目，弗吉尼亚州民主党众议员唐·拜尔(Don Beyer)周四在公开听证会上提出了这一点，当时他反对总统计划在纪念圈内修建纪念拱门，该纪念拱门直接穿过林肯纪念堂的纪念桥。
“从 1 月 3 日开始的拨款过程将由民主党控制。这将是国会议员拜尔介入的方式之一，”拜尔的发言人亚伦·弗里奇纳 (Aaron Fritschner) 表示。
众议院总法律顾问的任命将产生一个不太受重视的影响。众议院议长大概就是众议员哈基姆·杰弗里斯（Hakeem Jeffries）。
尽管民主党人加入了反对各种项目的诉讼，但他们的文件并不具有国会作为少数派的影响力。 “你会看到新的多数派正在拉动（众议院议长）迈克·约翰逊愿意放弃的权力平衡，”弗里奇纳说。
弗里奇纳说，拜尔已经成为批评者，并引用了在非当事人意见陈述中签名的其他成员。国家首都规划委员会会议持续了 9.5 个小时，一直持续到周四深夜，共有 120 多名证人出席。
该委员会以 8 比 4 的投票结果最终批准了这座 250 英尺（76 米）高的拱门，随后一名联邦法官在午夜前介入，阻止特朗普政府在 14 天内破土动工。

title_en: Cornell faculty declares ‘no confidence’ in school leaders in fallout from alleged gang-rape
title_zh: 康奈尔大学教师宣布对学校领导对涉嫌轮奸的后果“不信任”
summary: Faculty senate passed resolution expressing deep discontent with school’s response to alleged fraternity rape Cornell University’s faculty senate approved a resolution on Friday declaring “no confidence” in the school’s top leaders, a symbolic gesture reflecti
summary_zh: 康奈尔大学教职参议院通过决议，对学校对兄弟会强奸指控的反应表示深切不满
body_en: Faculty senate passed resolution expressing deep discontent with school’s response to alleged fraternity rape

Cornell University’s faculty senate approved a resolution on Friday declaring “no confidence” in the school’s top leaders, a symbolic gesture reflecting deep discontent on campus in the wake of a former student’s lawsuit saying she was gang-raped at a fraternity party in 2024.
The resolution passed 75-50, with five faculty senators abstaining and five others not voting, according to an email sent to members of the faculty senate on Friday afternoon.
Letitia James appoints ex-prosecutor to lead Cornell sexual assault investigation

The vote followed weeks of debate among professors over whether Cornell’s president, Michael Kotlikoff, and other administrators handled the woman’s allegations properly and whether they’ve done enough to curtail sexual misconduct at the prestigious university.

While the faculty body has no power over the university’s top leaders, backers of the resolution had said they hoped it would pressure Cornell’s trustees to urgently address what they viewed as longstanding institutional failures.
Voting took place electronically over more than a week, with the results released on Friday.

The board of trustees said on Friday that the vote reflected deep anger on campus and sent a “clear signal that what happened to Jane Doe is unacceptable”, but added that Kotlikoff and his administration were the right leaders to “thoughtfully and comprehensively” address the issue.

“The board fully supports President Kotlikoff and his administration as they continue to listen and act decisively in support of students,” board chair Anne Smalling said in a statement. She cited expanded sexual assault prevention education, additional victim advocates and more staff at the university’s office of civil rights as evidence of the administration’s response.

Thomas Giuffra, Jane Doe’s attorney, said in a statement on Friday that “we are hopeful that this will be yet another step forward to educate and support the Cornell community by addressing the longstanding scourge of sexual assault on campus.”

The Cornell community has been in a state of distress and dismay since mid-September, when a former student filed a lawsuit against the university and seven former members of the Chi Phi fraternity, saying she was given ketamine and raped at a fraternity house in October 2024.

All of those men have denied her allegations, saying that either the sex was consensual or they weren’t involved. The local district attorney initially decided the woman had consented to the encounter, and that no crime had been committed, but the investigation has since been reopened and handed to New York’s attorney general.

Cornell disciplined several of the accused students after a months long Title IX investigation. Two were expelled, two received suspensions and probation, and two were required to write “reflection” papers and complete bystander training. A seventh man had already graduated and was barred from campus, according to records obtained by the New York Times.
Kotlikoff also convened a taskforce to study the problem of sexual misconduct on campus, which released certain recommendations.
Some faculty members have been furious with Kotlikoff for not acting more forcefully to strengthen the school’s disciplinary process, push for criminal investigations and change campus party culture.
The no-confidence resolution did not call for Kotlikoff’s resignation.
body_zh: 教职参议院通过决议，对学校对兄弟会强奸指控的反应表示深切不满
康奈尔大学教师参议院周五批准了一项决议，宣布对学校最高领导人“不信任”，这一象征性举动反映了校园内因一名前学生在 2024 年在兄弟会聚会上被轮奸的诉讼而引发的深深不满。
根据周五下午发送给教职参议院成员的一封电子邮件，该决议以 75 比 50 的票数获得通过，其中 5 名教职参议员弃权，另外 5 名教职参议员没有投票。
利蒂西亚·詹姆斯任命前检察官领导康奈尔大学性侵犯调查
此次投票之前，教授们就康奈尔大学校长迈克尔·科特里科夫(Michael Kotlikoff)和其他管理人员是否妥善处理了这名女子的指控，以及他们是否采取了足够的措施来遏制这所著名大学的不当性行为进行了数周的辩论。
虽然教职员工团体对大学高层领导没有权力，但该决议的支持者表示，他们希望该决议能够向康奈尔大学的受托人施压，要求其紧急解决他们认为长期存在的机构失败问题。
投票以电子方式进行了一周多的时间，结果于周五公布。
董事会周五表示，这次投票反映了校园内的强烈愤怒，并发出了“明确的信号，表明发生在无名氏身上的事情是不可接受的”，但补充说，科特里科夫和他的政府是“深思熟虑和全面”解决这一问题的正确领导人。
董事会主席安妮·斯莫林（Anne Smalling）在一份声明中表示：“董事会完全支持科特利科夫总统和他的政府，他们将继续倾听并果断采取行动支持学生。”她列举了扩大性侵犯预防教育、增加受害者倡导者以及大学民权办公室增加工作人员作为政府应对措施的证据。
无名氏的律师托马斯·朱夫拉 (Thomas Giuffra) 在周五的一份声明中表示，“我们希望这将是通过解决校园内长期存在的性侵犯祸害，在教育和支持康奈尔大学社区方面又向前迈出的一步。”
自 9 月中旬以来，康奈尔大学社区一直处于痛苦和沮丧的状态，当时一名前学生对大学和 Chi Phi 兄弟会的七名前成员提起诉讼，称她于 2024 年 10 月在兄弟会会所中被给予氯胺酮并遭到强奸。
所有这些男人都否认了她的指控，称性行为要么是双方自愿的，要么他们没有参与。当地地方检察官最初判定该女子同意了这次遭遇，并且没有犯下任何犯罪行为，但此后调查已重新启动并移交给纽约总检察长。
经过一个月的第九条调查后，康奈尔大学对几名被指控的学生进行了纪律处分。两人被开除，两人被停职和缓刑，两人被要求写“反思”文件并完成旁观者培训。根据《纽约时报》获得的记录，第七名男子已经毕业并被禁止进入校园。
科特里科夫还召集了一个工作组来研究校园性行为不端问题，并发布了一些建议。
一些教职员工对科特里科夫没有采取更有力的行动来加强学校的纪律程序、推动刑事调查和改变校园党文化感到愤怒。
不信任决议并未要求科特利科夫辞职。

title_en: Three men charged in US with using AI to impersonate CEOs and steal millions
title_zh: 三名男子在美国被指控利用人工智能冒充首席执行官并窃取数百万美元
summary: Men allegedly impersonated voices and images of executives to convince employees to send large payments Three foreign nationals were arrested and charged with using AI to allegedly impersonate corporate CEOs and attorneys to steal over $100m, according to an i
summary_zh: 据称，男子冒充高管的声音和图像，说服员工支付大笔款项 三名外国人被捕并被烧毁
body_en: Men allegedly impersonated voices and images of executives to convince employees to send large payments

Three foreign nationals were arrested and charged with using AI to allegedly impersonate corporate CEOs and attorneys to steal over $100m, according to an indictment that was newly unsealed by the US Department of Justice.

According to a press release from the United States attorney’s office for the southern district of New York, three men – Jacob Soall, Sharon Hazan, and Guy Sheetrit – were arrested for using AI to alter and impersonate the voices and images of executives and attorneys at various companies in order to convince employees to send over large payments. Soall and Hazan were arrested in Spain over the summer, while Sheetrit was arrested in the United Kingdom in September. The alleged fraud took place between 2024 and 2026.

With the help of AI, the men allegedly acted as a corporate executive, targeting employees of various companies and telling them they needed their help with sensitive financial transactions. They would then instruct the employees to get in touch with lawyers at a large international law firm. The men would then impersonate a lawyer at these firms and have the employees wire a large amount of money.

The men ultimately stole more than $129m from companies all over the world including in the US, according to the DoJ. The men allegedly stole nearly $5m from a hospital system headquartered in Missouri; about $2.7m from a Rhode Island bank, about $3m from a California hospital system, over $4.6m from a mutual fund headquartered in Massachusetts and about $5m from a pet food company in Florida. The men also stole over $11m from a UK tech company.

The men would direct employees to wire money to bank accounts all over the world including in the United States, Spain , Portugal, Greece, the United Arab Emirates, Singapore, Austria, Slovakia and China. After the money had been wired, the men would covert the money into cryptocurrency “in an attempt to conceal the source, ownership, and control of the stolen proceeds and distributed it amongst themselves and their co-conspirators”, according to the DoJ press release. Soall and Hazan went by several aliases: Soal’s nicknames included “Seba Clarke” and “Rocky Balboa,” while Hazan went by “Superman Cash,” “Fat Boy,” and “Ron.”
In a statement, Jamie McDonald, a US attorney, said artificial intelligence had great potential but that the public should recognize that some may seek to use the technology to pursue criminal goals.

“The alleged scheme orchestrated by Soall, Hazan, and Sheetrit demonstrates how the use of advanced technology can be exploited to commit large-scale fraud,” said James C Barnacle Jr, the FBI assistant director in charge, in a statement. “As criminals continue to weaponize emerging technologies, the FBI remains committed to rapidly adapting our capabilities to identify, investigate, and disrupt those who seek to harm New Yorkers and businesses operating in our communities.”
The men have been charged with conspiracy to commit wire fraud, various counts of money-laundering conspiracy and aggravated identity theft.
body_zh: 据称，男子冒充高管的声音和图像来说服员工支付大笔款项
根据美国司法部最新公布的一份起诉书，三名外国人被捕，并被指控利用人工智能冒充企业首席执行官和律师窃取超过 1 亿美元。
根据纽约南区美国检察官办公室的一份新闻稿，三名男子——雅各布·索尔（Jacob Soall）、莎伦·哈赞（Sharon Hazan）和盖伊·谢特里特（Guy Sheetrit）——因使用人工智能改变和冒充多家公司高管和律师的声音和图像，以说服员工支付大笔款项而被捕。索尔和哈赞今年夏天在西班牙被捕，谢特里特则于 9 月在英国被捕。涉嫌欺诈发生在 2024 年至 2026 年期间。
据称，在人工智能的帮助下，这些人充当了公司高管，针对不同公司的员工，告诉他们在敏感的金融交易方面需要他们的帮助。然后他们会指示员工与一家大型国际律师事务所的律师取得联系。然后，这些人会冒充这些公司的律师，让员工汇出一大笔钱。

据美国司法部称，这些人最终从包括美国在内的世界各地公司窃取了超过 1.29 亿美元。据称，这些人从总部位于密苏里州的一家医院系统窃取了近 500 万美元；来自罗德岛州一家银行的约 270 万美元，来自加利福尼亚州医院系统的约 300 万美元，来自总部位于马萨诸塞州的共同基金的超过 460 万美元，来自佛罗里达州一家宠物食品公司的约 500 万美元。这些人还从一家英国科技公司窃取了超过 1100 万美元。
这些人将指导员工将钱汇入世界各地的银行账户，包括美国、西班牙、葡萄牙、希腊、阿拉伯联合酋长国、新加坡、奥地利、斯洛伐克和中国。根据司法部的新闻稿，这些人在电汇后，会将钱转换成加密货币，“试图隐藏被盗收益的来源、所有权和控制权，并将其分配给他们自己及其同谋”。索尔和哈赞有几个别名：索尔的绰号包括“塞巴·克拉克”和“洛基·巴尔博亚”，而哈赞则有“超人卡什”、“胖男孩”和“罗恩”。
美国律师杰米·麦克唐纳在一份声明中表示，人工智能具有巨大潜力，但公众应该认识到，有些人可能会寻求利用该技术来实现犯罪目标。
联邦调查局负责助理局长詹姆斯·C·巴纳克尔 (James C Barnacle Jr) 在一份声明中表示：“索尔、哈赞和谢特里特精心策划的所谓计划展示了如何利用先进技术实施大规模欺诈。” “随着犯罪分子继续将新兴技术武器化，联邦调查局仍然致力于迅速调整我们的能力，以识别、调查和瓦解那些试图伤害纽约人和在我们社区运营的企业的人。”
这些人被指控串谋实施电信诈骗、串谋洗钱和严重身份盗窃等多项罪名。

title_en: Democrats win the Arizona House, Senate and governor's office for the first time since 1966
title_zh: 民主党自 1966 年以来首次赢得亚利桑那州众议院、参议院和州长职位
summary: The Associated Press called enough legislative races to confirm that both chambers flipped on Friday.
summary_zh: 美联社称，进行了足够多的立法竞选，以确认参众两院在周五发生了翻转。
body_en: https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/democrats-win-the-arizona-house-senate-and-governors-office-for-the-first-time-since-1966

PHOENIX (AP) — Democrats in Arizona won control of both state legislative chambers and retained the governor's office, giving the party its first trifecta in the state since 1966 as Democrats made major gains nationwide in this week's elections and took control of both chambers of Congress.

In her first term, Democratic Gov. Katie Hobbs had vetoed more than 540 measures passed by the Republican-led Legislature on policies including taxes, immigration and voting laws. Hobbs has said she's looking to address water issues and affordability, and take on fraud and abuse in the state's school voucher program.

The Associated Press called enough legislative races to confirm that both chambers flipped on Friday. The news organization calls races individually and it can take several days after voting, depending on when election officials tally the votes and how close the elections are. There have not been major disputes or disruptions this year.
In Arizona, Republicans have held the House for 60 years and the Senate since the early 1990s.

Overall, Democrats took full control — both statehouse chambers and governors' offices — in at least six states where they previously shared power with Republicans. Besides Arizona, those wins were in the battleground states of Michigan, Minnesota, Pennsylvania, Nevada and Wisconsin.

The flips weren't just in states that are normally competitive. Democrats won control of the Texas House, which Republicans have held since 2003, and elected Gina Hinojosa as the state's first Democratic governor since George W. Bush ousted Ann Richards in 1994. Republicans held onto the state Senate.

Democrats also flipped the lower chambers of the legislatures in Maine and North Carolina and both chambers in New Hampshire, where Republican Kelly Ayotte was reelected. The count could grow as results are tallied in additional states.

The National Council of State Legislatures says it's likely to end up as the election with the most legislative seats and chambers changing parties since the 2010 election, when Republicans took over governments across the country amid the Great Recession.
Democrats will also hold the governor's office in at least 28 states. Results are still pending in Alaska and Kansas.

body_zh: 菲尼克斯（美联社）——亚利桑那州的民主党赢得了州议会两院的控制权，并保住了州长职位，民主党在本周的选举中在全国范围内取得了重大进展，并控制了国会两院，这使得该党自 1966 年以来在该州首次取得三连胜。
民主党州长凯蒂·霍布斯 (Katie Hobbs) 在其第一个任期内否决了共和党领导的立法机构通过的 540 多项税收、移民和投票法等政策措施。霍布斯表示，她正在寻求解决水问题和负担能力问题，并打击该州学校优惠券计划中的欺诈和滥用行为。
美联社称，进行了足够多的立法竞选，以确认参众两院在周五发生了翻转。该新闻机构对竞选进行个别报道，投票后可能需要几天时间，具体取决于选举官员统计选票的时间以及选举结果的接近程度。今年没有发生重大纠纷或干扰。
在亚利桑那州，共和党已经控制众议院 60 年，自 20 世纪 90 年代初以来一直控制参议院。
总体而言，民主党在之前与共和党分享权力的至少六个州完全控制了州议会厅和州长办公室。除亚利桑那州外，这些胜利还发生在密歇根州、明尼苏达州、宾夕法尼亚州、内华达州和威斯康星州等战场州。
这种翻转不仅仅发生在通常竞争激烈的州。民主党赢得了共和党自 2003 年以来一直控制的德克萨斯州众议院的控制权，并选举吉娜·伊诺霍萨 (Gina Hinojosa) 为自 1994 年乔治·W·布什 (George W. Bush) 驱逐安·理查兹 (Ann Richards) 以来该州第一位民主党州长。共和党保住了州参议院。
民主党还推翻了缅因州和北卡罗来纳州的下议院以及新罕布什尔州的两院，共和党人凯利·阿约特在新罕布什尔州再次当选。随着更多州统计结果，这一数字可能会增加。
全国州立法机构委员会表示，这次选举很可能是自 2010 年大选以来立法席位和众议院更换党派最多的一次选举，当时共和党在大衰退期间接管了全国各地的政府。
民主党还将在至少 28 个州担任州长职务。阿拉斯加和堪萨斯州的结果仍在等待中。

title_en: Several Democrats renew calls for datacenter pauses after blue wave
title_zh: 几名民主党人再次呼吁在蓝色浪潮后暂停数据中心
summary: Tech industry fears delays to its multi-trillion dollar infrastructure buildout meant to power artificial intelligence Several newly elected Democrats and Senator Bernie Sanders have renewed calls for datacenter moratoriums in the days after the US midterm ele
summary_zh: 科技行业担心其数万亿美元的基础设施建设计划会被推迟，该基础设施建设旨在为人工智能提供动力 几位新当选的民主党人
body_en: Several Democrats renew calls for datacenter pauses after blue wave | Datacenters – US
Tech industry fears delays to its multi-trillion dollar infrastructure buildout meant to power artificial intelligence

Several newly elected Democrats and Senator Bernie Sanders have renewed calls for datacenter moratoriums in the days after the US midterm elections. The sweeping Democratic victory , which was buoyed in part by backlash to the tech industry , has added momentum to efforts to slow down the multi-trillion-dollar buildout of the controversial facilities.

On the social media platform X, Sanders posted a call for an immediate national datacenter moratorium this week. “Americans don’t want Big Tech oligarchs wrecking the environment, gutting jobs and threatening humanity’s future,” Sanders said on Wednesday.
Sanders was joined by several Democrats , including Representative Yassamin Ansari of Arizona – a state where Elon Musk’s SpaceX has proposed a datacenter project that would span more than 700 acres.

“Top of the Democratic agenda on day 1 needs to be a pause on advanced AI development, regulation of this out of control industry, and a ban on artificial superintelligence,” Ansari posted Wednesday on X. Musk mocked her post in a retweet, and the two sparred, with Ansari forecasting congressional hearings, telling the centi-billionaire: “See you soon.”
Datacenters were on the ballot. US voters rejected them

The pushback to the buildout of datacenters, which tech companies need to power the AI products that have become central to their businesses, was one of the most visible issues of the midterms. Opposition to datacenters figured heavily in campaigns across the US, while voters passed dozens of local ballot measures aimed at restricting datacenter projects in their states.

The outcome of the midterm elections has so far alarmed tech investors and executives, with Meta platforms president Dina Powell McCormick telling the Wall Street Journal that it is “going to be harder” to build datacenters following the vote. After Elon Musk spent nearly half a billion dollars backing Republican candidates and attacking Democrats on his social media platform, he jokingly posted on election night that “datacenters in space looking pretty appealing right now.”

Post-midterms anxiety also helped fuel a massive selloff of AI stocks this week, as tech investors worried about new regulation such as datacenter pauses. White House National Economic Council director Kevin Hassett was confident that the construction of datacenters would continue, however, arguing to CNBC that the ballot initiatives largely wouldn’t affect existing projects.

Datacenters and AI opposition featured in numerous Democratic victory speeches after midterms, as newly elected representatives vowed to curb the power of Big Tech. In New Hampshire, Senator-elect Chris Pappas praised his constituents for “opposing big data centers that harm our communities”. New Mexico congressman Gabe Vasquez meanwhile proclaimed “the time is now to stop the AI billionaire class from forcing datacenters in our community.”
Several victorious Democratic candidates also promised that they would hand local communities the decision-making power over AI and data centers.
“I do not work for data centers,” Ohio Senator-elect Sherrod Brown said to applause. “I work for you. I work for Ohio.”

Newly elected governors in several states key to the datacenter buildout, including Texas and Georgia, have also called for moratoriums on datacenters. Incoming Texas Governor Gina Hinojosa, whose state has become a hotspot for datacenter construction, pledged to halt new datacenter projects until new protections are in place.

“There are no rules and laws to protect Texans, and Texans are being taken advantage of,” Hinojosa said this week on CNN . “We need to stop what we are doing with data centers until we have those protections.”
body_zh: 几名民主党人再次呼吁在蓝色浪潮之后暂停数据中心 |数据中心 – 美国
科技行业担心其数万亿美元的基础设施建设计划会被推迟，该基础设施建设旨在为人工智能提供动力
几位新当选的民主党人和参议员伯尼·桑德斯在美国中期选举后的几天内再次呼吁暂停数据中心。民主党的压倒性胜利，在一定程度上是由于科技行业的强烈反对，为减缓有争议的设施的数万亿美元建设的努力增添了动力。
桑德斯本周在社交媒体平台 X 上呼吁立即暂停全国数据中心。桑德斯周三表示：“美国人不希望大型科技寡头破坏环境、减少就业机会并威胁人类的未来。”
几位民主党人也加入了桑德斯的行列，其中包括亚利桑那州众议员亚萨明·安萨里 (Yassamin Ansari)，埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 的 SpaceX 已在该州提议建设一个占地 700 多英亩的数据中心项目。
安萨里周三在 X 上发帖称，“民主党第一天议程的首要任务是暂停先进人工智能的开发、监管这个失控的行业，以及禁止人工智能。”马斯克在转发中嘲笑了她的帖子，两人发生争执，安萨里预测国会听证会，告诉这位百亿富翁：“很快见。”
数据中心也在选票上。美国选民拒绝了他们
科技公司需要数据中心来为已成为其业务核心的人工智能产品提供动力，而对数据中心建设的抵制是中期选举中最明显的问题之一。对数据中心的反对在美国各地的竞选活动中占据重要地位，而选民们通过了数十项旨在限制本州数据中心项目的地方投票措施。
中期选举的结果迄今为止已经让科技投资者和高管感到震惊，Meta 平台总裁迪娜·鲍威尔·麦考密克 (Dina Powell McCormick) 告诉《华尔街日报》，投票后建设数据中心“将变得更加困难”。在埃隆·马斯克花费近 5 亿美元支持共和党候选人并在其社交媒体平台上攻击民主党后，他在选举之夜开玩笑地表示，“太空数据中心现在看起来相当有吸引力”。
中期选举后的焦虑也助长了本周人工智能股票的大规模抛售，因为科技投资者担心数据中心暂停等新监管。然而，白宫国家经济委员会主任凯文·哈塞特 (Kevin Hassett) 对数据中心的建设将继续进行充满信心，他向 CNBC 表示，投票举措很大程度上不会影响现有项目。
中期选举后，数据中心和人工智能的反对派出现在许多民主党获胜演讲中，新当选的代表发誓要遏制大型科技公司的力量。在新罕布什尔州，当选参议员克里斯·帕帕斯赞扬他的选民“反对损害我们社区的大数据中心”。与此同时，新墨西哥州国会议员 Gabe Vasquez 宣称“现在是时候阻止人工智能亿万富翁阶层在我们的社区中强行建立数据中心了。”
几位获胜的民主党候选人还承诺，他们将把人工智能和数据中心的决策权交给当地社区。
“我不为数据中心工作，”俄亥俄州当选参议员谢罗德·布朗说道，赢得了掌声。 “我为你工作。我为俄亥俄州工作。”
德克萨斯州和佐治亚州等对数据中心建设至关重要的几个州新当选的州长也呼吁暂停数据中心建设。即将上任的德克萨斯州州长吉娜·伊诺霍萨（Gina Hinojosa）承诺，在新的保护措施到位之前，将停止新的数据中心项目。该州已成为数据中心建设的热点。
“没有任何规则和法律来保护德克萨斯人，德克萨斯人正在被利用，”伊诺霍萨本周在美国有线电视新闻网 (CNN) 上表示。 “我们需要停止对数据中心所做的事情，直到我们得到这些保护。”

title_en: South Florida candidate sues election official, alleging bias in a contentious, razor-thin race
title_zh: 南佛罗里达州候选人起诉选举官员，指控在一场有争议的、微弱的竞选中存在偏见
summary: MIAMI — South Florida Democratic congressional candidate Eliott Rodriguez filed a federal lawsuit against the Miami-Dade supervisor of elections Friday, citing bias after she declined to recuse herself from the recount process.
summary_zh: 迈阿密——南佛罗里达州民主党国会候选人埃利奥特·罗德里格斯对迈阿密戴德县选举监督员弗里达提起联邦诉讼
body_en: MIAMI — South Florida Democratic congressional candidate Eliott Rodriguez filed a federal lawsuit against the Miami-Dade supervisor of elections Friday, citing bias after she declined to recuse herself from the recount process. Incumbent Rep. Maria Elvira Salazar is named in the lawsuit as well.

The lawsuit seeks to bar Miami-Dade supervisor of elections, Alina García, from acting as a deciding member of the county canvassing board for the 27th Congressional District, where the results are razor-thin.

Salazar was leading Rodriguez by 1,103 votes or 0.44 percentage points as of Thursday evening. Florida law requires automatic recounts when there is less than a 0.5-point margin. The canvassing board oversees the recount.
Rodriguez’s campaign demanded Thursday that García recuse herself from oversight of the recount.

The Rodriguez campaign alleged the attorney representing Salazar in the recount, Robert Fernández, is García’s son-in-law and requested immediate confirmation, saying the relationship would raise additional serious concerns, according to the complaint.

The campaign also cited in the lawsuit an interview García gave to The Miami Herald on election night stating, “Maria Elvira is the winner, with or without a recount” and that it was “possible but not probable” there were enough remaining ballots to flip the results.

She added that recounts almost never end up going the other way. “Usually the trend we see is what continues,” García was quoted as saying. In other words, if Salazar is ahead, it will likely remain that way.

The Miami Herald also reported that Oren Rosenthal, general counsel for the supervisor of elections, estimated he’s seen about 20 recounts, and with the margin that Salazar was leading by on Tuesday night, he said it was unlikely the result will be overturned.

In a press release, García stated, “I want to reiterate that I was elected by the people to perform the duties of the Supervisor of Elections. Nothing disqualifies me form performing those duties including serving on the Canvassing Board. Accordingly, as I have stated previously, I have not recused myself, nor will I.”
Juan-Carlos Planas, general counsel for the Miami-Dade Democratic Executive Committee, ran against García in the 2024 supervisor of elections race.

“If candidates are going to hire relatives from the supervisor of elections, we’re going down a very dangerous precedent,” he said. “Can you imagine going into court and litigants are hiring relatives of the judge? The judge would be removed from office.”

On Thursday evening, the day before the final counting of ballots and certification of results was scheduled to take place, an attorney representing Rodriguez sent a letter to García demanding she step away from matters involving the race.

“This goes beyond any ethical standards. The canvassing board is a quasi-judicial body so she sits as a quasi-judicial official,” Planas said. “This is a quasi-judicial body and therefore she should recuse herself like any other judge would.”

García, a Republican who served one term in the Florida state House before winning the election for supervisor of elections in 2024, has posed in pictures with fellow Republican leaders, including Salazar and President Donald Trump . She is the first elected supervisor of elections. It was previously a nonpartisan position appointed by the county’s mayor.
Few pundits considered the race competitive this time around, but the district shifted 14.26 points toward Democrats compared with the 2024 presidential election.
Salazar’s office did not respond to a request for comment.
“My opponent is behaving like an election denier, attempting to turn this process into a political circus because he does not like election outcome,” Salazar posted on X Thursday night.

Salazar and Rodriguez are both Cuban American and former journalists. Salazár has won three consecutive terms to represent the heavily Hispanic 27th Congressional District. She and Trump comfortably won the district in 2024.
There were signs of trouble for Salazar in September when she released an ad where she broke with Trump on his immigration policies.
“Mr. President, some of your immigration enforcement efforts have gone too far,” she said in the ad while standing in front of the White House.
body_zh: 迈阿密——周五，南佛罗里达州民主党国会候选人埃利奥特·罗德里格斯(Eliot Rodriguez)对迈阿密戴德县选举监督员提起联邦诉讼，理由是她拒绝回避重新计票程序后存在偏见。现任众议员玛丽亚·埃尔维拉·萨拉查也在诉讼中被点名。
该诉讼旨在禁止迈阿密戴德县选举监督员阿丽娜·加西亚 (Alina García) 担任第 27 国会选区县拉票委员会的决定性成员，该选区的选举结果微乎其微。
截至周四晚上，萨拉查领先罗德里格斯 1,103 票，即 0.44 个百分点。佛罗里达州法律要求当差距小于 0.5 分时自动重新计票。拉票委员会监督重新计票。
罗德里格斯的竞选团队周四要求加西亚回避重新计票的监督。
起诉书称，罗德里格斯竞选团队声称，在重新计票中代表萨拉查的律师罗伯特·费尔南德斯是加西亚的女婿，并要求立即确认，称这种关系将引起更多严重担忧。
竞选团队还在诉讼中引用了加西亚在选举之夜接受《迈阿密先驱报》采访时所说的内容，称“无论重新计票与否，玛丽亚·埃尔维拉都是赢家”，并且“有可能但不太可能”有足够的剩余选票来推翻结果。
她补充说，重述几乎永远不会以相反的方式结束。加西亚表示：“通常我们看到的趋势就会持续下去。”换句话说，如果萨拉查领先，那么情况很可能会保持下去。
《迈阿密先驱报》还报道称，选举监督员总法律顾问奥伦·罗森塔尔估计，他已经看到了大约 20 次重新计票，而且鉴于萨拉查周二晚上的领先优势，他表示结果不太可能被推翻。
加西亚在一份新闻稿中表示，“我想重申，我是由人民选举产生的，是为了履行选举监督员的职责。没有任何事情可以阻止我履行这些职责，包括在拉票委员会任职。因此，正如我之前所说，我没有、也不会回避。”
迈阿密戴德县民主党执行委员会总法律顾问胡安-卡洛斯·普拉纳斯 (Juan-Carlos Planas) 在 2024 年选举监督员竞选中与加西亚竞争。
他说：“如果候选人要聘请选举主管的亲属，我们将开创一个非常危险的先例。” “你能想象进入法庭时诉讼当事人正在雇佣法官的亲属吗？法官将被免职。”
周四晚上，即最终计票和结果认证的前一天，罗德里格斯的代表律师致信加西亚，要求她退出涉及竞选的事务。
“这超出了任何道德标准。拉票委员会是一个准司法机构，因此她是一名准司法官员，”普拉纳斯说。 “这是一个准司法机构，因此她应该像其他法官一样回避。”
加西亚是一名共和党人，在赢得 2024 年选举监督员选举之前曾在佛罗里达州众议院任职一届，他曾与萨拉查和唐纳德·特朗普总统等共和党领导人合影。她是第一位当选的选举监督员。此前，该职位是由县长任命的无党派职位。
很少有专家认为这次竞选具有竞争力，但与 2024 年总统选举相比，该选区向民主党倾斜了 14.26 个百分点。
萨拉查的办公室没有回应置评请求。
“我的对手的行为就像一个选举否认者，试图将这一过程变成一场政治马戏团，因为他不喜欢选举结果，”萨拉查在星期四晚上的 X 上发帖说。
萨拉查和罗德里格斯都是古巴裔美国人，都曾是记者。萨拉萨尔已连续赢得三届任期，代表西班牙裔人口较多的第 27 国会选区。她和特朗普在 2024 年轻松赢得了该选区。
9月份，萨拉查发布了一则广告，在广告中与特朗普在移民政策上发生了分歧，这给她带来了麻烦。
“总统先生，你们的一些移民执法工作做得太过分了，”她站在白宫前在广告中说道。

title_en: Cornell faculty senate votes no confidence in administration’s handling of sexual assault
title_zh: 康奈尔大学教师参议院对政府处理性侵犯的方式不信任
summary: Members of the Cornell University faculty senate on Friday issued a vote of no confidence in the administration’s ability to manage the response to an alleged sexual assault at a fraternity house in 2024, according to the university.
summary_zh: 康奈尔大学教职参议院成员周五对政府应对疫情的能力投了不信任票。
body_en: Nov. 6, 2026, 3:54 PM EST / Updated Nov. 6, 2026, 5:41 PM EST

Members of the Cornell University faculty senate on Friday issued a vote of no confidence in the administration’s ability to manage the response to an alleged sexual assault at a fraternity house in 2024, according to the university.

The governing body took up the issue after a former student, known as Jane Doe, alleged she was sexually assaulted and forced to take drugs at the Chi Phi fraternity house from Oct. 19 to 20, 2024. The allegations, detailed in a lawsuit the woman filed in September, led to widespread criticism of the university and calls for reform from students and alumni.
The senate’s resolution states that the body “has no confidence in the ability of the central administration to effectively address the ongoing crisis of sexual assault at Cornell University.”

It does not recommend removals or suggest how to manage the controversy’s fallout. It passed by a vote of 75-50, with five abstentions and five members not voting, according to a copy of the results obtained by NBC News.
Former Cornell student alleging sexual assault addressed faculty senate in letter

The vote will not directly affect leadership decisions at the institution, including whether President Michael Kotlikoff remains in his role. The board of trustees, which has the authority to replace him, can consider the finding in its decisions but suggested in a statement Friday that no immediate changes were expected.

“The Board of Trustees remains confident that President Kotlikoff and his administration are the right leaders to thoughtfully and comprehensively address the serious problem of sexual assault on our campus,” chair Anne Meinig Smalling said.
Smalling highlighted recent changes implemented by leadership.

“They have already taken several important steps to this end, including adding staff to the Cornell Office of Civil Rights, expanding in-person sexual assault prevention education, and hiring more victim advocates,” Smalling said. “The administration will continue to build on that progress with more initiatives to be launched in the weeks and months ahead.”
Faculty senators who sponsored the resolution called the decision “a reckoning” for the university.

“It is a call for real, systemic change; not a slow-moving taskforce, weakly enforced ban on fraternity parties, or expensive [public relations] damage control, but meaningful, evidence-based steps to reduce the incidence of sexual assault on campus and provide significant support to and justice for survivors,” the sponsors wrote in a statement.
Jane Doe and her attorney have alleged that Cornell failed to support her through the reporting process and subsequent investigation.

“We are hopeful that this will be yet another step forward to educate and support the Cornell community by addressing the longstanding scourge of sexual assault on campus,” said Jane Doe’s attorney Thomas Giuffra.
Jane Doe accused seven members of the fraternity of participating in a sexual assault, which she told police began with a consensual threesome but resulted in unwanted sex and ketamine consumption.
All seven men accused in the incident deny the allegations. Two were expelled from the university after an internal civil rights proceeding, and others faced less severe punishments from the school.
Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten said he declined to pursue a criminal case in November 2024 based on a six-page statement from Jane Doe.

New York Attorney General Letitia James was appointed by Gov. Kathy Hochul last month to investigate the matter and consider whether criminal charges are supported. Two of the defendants initiated court proceedings aimed at disqualifying James based on what they argue are biased statements of support for Jane Doe that James posted on social media.

On Thursday, several defendants joined an Article 78 proceeding in Sullivan County that was recently filed by lawyers for one of the fraternity brothers, Gillio Lopes. Diego Sarabia, Scott Kretzschmar, Scott Norris and Winston Lee, who are co-defendants in Jane Doe’s lawsuit, were added to the petition in support of Lopes’ request.
Two remaining defendants, Matthew Ingalls and Jonathan Newell, do not have representation in the civil case and did not respond to Lopes’ attorneys.
body_zh: 美国东部时间 2026 年 11 月 6 日下午 3:54 / 更新于美国东部时间 2026 年 11 月 6 日下午 5:41
据康奈尔大学称，周五，康奈尔大学教师参议院成员对政府应对 2024 年兄弟会会所涉嫌性侵犯事件的能力投了不信任票。
一名名叫 Jane Doe 的前学生声称，她于 2024 年 10 月 19 日至 20 日在 Chi Phi 兄弟会所遭到性侵犯并被迫吸毒。该女子在 9 月份提起的诉讼中详细说明了这些指控，引发了对该大学的广泛批评，并呼吁学生和校友进行改革。
参议院的决议指出，该机构“对中央政府有效解决康奈尔大学持续存在的性侵犯危机的能力没有信心”。
它不建议删除或建议如何管理争议的后果。根据 NBC 新闻获得的投票结果副本，会议以 75 票对 50 票通过，五票弃权，五名成员未投票。
指控性侵犯的前康奈尔大学学生致信教员参议院
这次投票不会直接影响该机构的领导决策，包括校长迈克尔·科特利科夫是否继续担任其职务。有权接替他的董事会可以在其决定中考虑这一发现，但在周五的一份声明中表示，预计不会立即做出改变。
董事会主席安妮·梅尼格·斯莫林 (Anne Meinig Smalling) 表示：“董事会仍然相信，科特利科夫校长和他的政府是正确的领导者，能够深思熟虑、全面地解决我们校园中严重的性侵犯问题。”
斯莫林强调了领导层最近实施的变革。
斯莫林说：“他们已经为此采取了几项重要措施，包括向康奈尔大学民权办公室增加工作人员，扩大面对面的性侵犯预防教育，以及雇用更多的受害者倡导者。” “政府将继续在这一进展的基础上，在未来几周和几个月内推出更多举措。”
支持该决议的教职参议员称该决定是对大学的“清算”。
赞助商在一份声明中写道：“这是对真正的、系统性变革的呼吁；不是行动缓慢的工作组，对兄弟会聚会的禁令执行不力，也不是昂贵的[公共关系]损害控制，而是采取有意义的、基于证据的措施，以减少校园性侵犯的发生率，并为幸存者提供重要的支持和正义。”
无名氏和她的律师声称康奈尔大学未能在报告过程和随后的调查中为她提供支持。
“我们希望，通过解决校园内长期存在的性侵犯祸害，这将成为教育和支持康奈尔大学社区的又一步，”无名氏的律师托马斯·朱弗拉说。
无名氏指控该兄弟会的七名成员参与了性侵犯，她告诉警方，这起性侵犯始于双方同意的三人行，但导致了不必要的性行为和服用氯胺酮。
事件中被指控的七名男子全部否认这些指控。两人在内部民权诉讼后被学校开除，其他人则受到学校较轻的处罚。
汤普金斯县地方检察官 Matthew Van Houten 表示，根据 Jane Doe 的六页声明，他拒绝在 2024 年 11 月提起刑事诉讼。
纽约州总检察长利蒂西亚·詹姆斯 (Letitia James) 上个月被州长凯西·霍赫尔 (Kathy Hochul) 任命，负责调查此事并考虑刑事指控是否得到支持。两名被告提起法庭诉讼，旨在取消詹姆斯的资格，因为他们认为詹姆斯在社交媒体上发布的支持无名氏的言论带有偏见。

周四，几名被告参加了沙利文县的第 78 条诉讼，该诉讼最近由兄弟会兄弟之一吉利奥·洛佩斯 (Gillio Lopes) 的律师提起。 Jane Doe 诉讼中的共同被告迭戈·萨拉比亚 (Diego Sarabia)、斯科特·克雷茨施马尔 (Scott Kretzschmar)、斯科特·诺里斯 (Scott Norris) 和温斯顿·李 (Winston Lee) 也被添加到请愿书中，以支持洛佩斯的请求。
剩下的两名被告马修·英格尔斯和乔纳森·纽厄尔在民事案件中没有代表，也没有对洛佩斯的律师做出回应。

title_en: Israel's Arab-led parties in spotlight after inconclusive election
title_zh: 以色列阿拉伯领导的政党在选举无果后成为焦点
summary: Israel's center-right opposition has a chance to unseat Netanyahu — but backing of Arab-led parties will be key.
summary_zh: 以色列中右翼反对派有机会推翻内塔尼亚胡，但阿拉伯领导政党的支持将是关键。
body_en: Israel's Palestinian citizens vote in record numbers : NPR
Israel's Palestinian citizens vote in record numbers Israel's center-right opposition has a chance to unseat Netanyahu — but backing of Arab-led parties will be key.
Arab parties hold the key to power in deadlocked Israel election
A Palestinian citizen of Israel casts her ballot in the country's general election at a polling station in Umm al-Fahm, Israel, Oct. 27, 2026 Mahmoud Illean/AP hide caption

KUFR QASI, Israel — In recent years many Palestinian citizens of Israel shunned elections, believing there was little to gain from participating in the politics of a state which, they say, regularly marginalizes their communities and oppresses their fellow Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza.

But last month, Palestinian Arabs in Israel came to the ballot boxes in record numbers, helping strip Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's most far-right government in Israel's history of its majority, and giving Arab-led parties the votes they needed to become a powerful force in Israeli politics.

"We blocked the government of Netanyahu from continuing," said Jamal Zahalka, chairman of the High Follow-Up Committee, the main umbrella body representing Palestinian citizens of Israel. "It's a historical achievement. I think our community found its strength."

Neither Netanyahu's coalition, nor his main challenger Gadi Eisenkot's center-right opposition, reached the threshold of 61 seats needed to form a government. Arab-led parties won 19 out of 120 seats — enough to give them a critical role in the negotiations that will now determine who governs Israel at this turbulent moment in the country's history.
The election results strike at the heart of the decades-long questions about how Israel defines itself and the role of Palestinian Arabs in its society.

At a park in the Palestinian-majority town of Kufr Qasim two days after the election, hundreds of people gathered for the annual commemoration of residents gunned down in 1956 by Israeli border police on the opening day of the Suez Crisis in the violent early years of the state, when Israel, Britain and France attacked Egypt after it nationalized the Suez Canal.
"And today we stand here, 70 years later," the speaker told the large crowd from a podium: "And the story still isn't over."

The crowd at this event, mostly dressed in black — some wearing the keffiyeh, the black and white stitched scarf symbolizing Palestinian resistance — mourned not only their lost relatives all those years ago, but also the suffering of Palestinians now: the sharp rise in discrimination against their communities in Israel since the deadly Hamas-led attacks on Israel on Oct. 7, 2023; Israel's war against Hamas in Gaza that has killed more than 74,000 Palestinians and left a population to survive amid the ruins of the enclave. And the actions of Netanyahu's extreme right-wing government in the occupied West Bank, where rights groups and the U.N. say it has armed and supported settlers as they force Palestinians from their homes and agricultural lands with unprecedented violence.
Our reporter witnesses the largest detention of West Bank activists in a decade

Worsening rights inside Israel was one reason, residents of Kufr Qasm told NPR, why so many Palestinian citizens in Israel went to the ballot boxes. "There is no freedom anymore," said Intisar Sarsur, 65, sitting with relatives beside an olive tree in the park in Kufr Qasim. " We are seeking for our basic rights as human beings."

"Everybody that I know participated in the elections. Not one person stayed home," Sarsur said. She and her family were sharing platters of mutabbaq , a sweet Palestinian layered pastry, and freshly pressed olive oil from this year's olive harvest — usually a joyous moment in the Palestinian calendar, that she said now felt bittersweet. This year the olive harvest for Palestinians in the occupied West Bank was marred by frequent attacks by Israeli settlers trying to disrupt this economically and culturally significant time of year.

Mansour Abbas, a lawmaker in Israel's parliament and leader of the conservative Muslim Ra'am party, embraces a supporter after the release of the first exit poll results in Israel's general election in Sakhnin, Israel, on Oct. 27. Mahmoud Illean/AP hide caption

Palestinian citizens of Israel, descendants of those who remained as the state of Israel was established in 1948 (when a majority of the prewar population was forcibly expelled or fled during the war) now make up about 20% of the population.

This election, Arab-led parties received a 64% increase in votes compared to the last elections, according to the Central Elections Committee. The gains they made have stirred anger, and even fear, among many on Israel's political right, who see them as a threat to the country's Jewish character.

Netanyahu and his allies made the large Arab turnout a rallying cry. On election day, Netanyahu posted a video calling it an "emergency." Itamar Ben Gvir, the far-right national security minister, filmed his own appeal at the entrance to Kufr Qasim: "If you want this country to remain Jewish and Zionist … then get out and vote!"
body_zh: 以色列巴勒斯坦公民投票人数创历史新高：NPR
以色列的巴勒斯坦公民投票人数创历史新高以色列的中右翼反对派有机会推翻内塔尼亚胡，但阿拉伯领导的政党的支持将是关键。
以色列选举陷入僵局，阿拉伯政党掌握权力关键
2026 年 10 月 27 日，一名以色列巴勒斯坦公民在以色列乌姆法姆的一个投票站为该国大选投票 Mahmoud Illean/美联社 隐藏标题栏
以色列库弗尔卡西——近年来，许多以色列巴勒斯坦公民回避选举，认为参与一个国家的政治没有什么好处，他们说，这个国家经常边缘化他们的社区，并压迫约旦河西岸和加沙的巴勒斯坦同胞。
但上个月，以色列的巴勒斯坦阿拉伯人以创纪录的数量来到投票箱，帮助以色列总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡（Benjamin Netanyahu）剥夺了以色列历史上最右翼政府的多数席位，并为阿拉伯领导的政党提供了成为以色列政治中强大力量所需的选票。
“我们阻止内塔尼亚胡政府继续执政，”代表以色列巴勒斯坦公民的主要保护伞机构高级后续委员会主席贾马尔·扎哈卡说。 “这是一项历史性成就。我认为我们的社区找到了自己的力量。”
内塔尼亚胡的联盟及其主要挑战者加迪·艾森科特的中右翼反对派都没有达到组建政府所需的 61 个席位的门槛。阿拉伯领导的政党赢得了 120 个席位中的 19 个，这足以使它们在谈判中发挥关键作用，而谈判现在将决定谁在以色列历史上这个动荡的时刻统治以色列。
选举结果触及了数十年来以色列如何定义自己以及巴勒斯坦阿拉伯人在其社会中的角色等问题的核心。
选举两天后，在巴勒斯坦人占多数的库夫尔卡西姆镇的一个公园里，数百人聚集在一起，参加一年一度的纪念活动，纪念1956年苏伊士危机爆发当天被以色列边防警察枪杀的居民，当时以色列、英国和法国在埃及将苏伊士运河收归国有后袭击了埃及。
“70 年后的今天，我们站在这里，”演讲者在讲台上对一大群人说道，“故事还没有结束。”

参加这次活动的人群大多身着黑衣，其中一些人戴着阿拉伯头巾，这是一种象征巴勒斯坦抵抗的黑白缝制围巾，他们不仅哀悼多年前失去的亲人，也哀悼巴勒斯坦人现在所遭受的苦难：自 2023 年 10 月 7 日哈马斯领导的对以色列发动致命袭击以来，以色列境内对其社区的歧视急剧增加；以色列在加沙对哈马斯发动的战争已造成 74,000 多名巴勒斯坦人死亡，只剩下一些人在飞地的废墟中生存。还有内塔尼亚胡极右翼政府在被占领的约旦河西岸的行动，人权组织和联合国表示，内塔尼亚胡政府武装并支持定居者，以前所未有的暴力迫使巴勒斯坦人离开家园和农田。
我们的记者目睹了十年来最大规模的西岸活动人士被拘留
库夫尔·卡斯姆的居民告诉美国公共广播电台，以色列境内人权状况恶化是众多以色列巴勒斯坦公民前往投票箱的原因之一。 “不再有自由了，”65 岁的因蒂萨尔·萨尔苏尔 (Intisar Sarsur) 说，他和亲戚坐在库夫卡西姆公园的一棵橄榄树旁。 “我们正在寻求作为人类的基本权利。”
“我认识的每个人都参加了选举。没有人呆在家里，”萨苏尔说。她和她的家人正在分享一盘 mutabbaq（一种甜美的巴勒斯坦分层糕点）和今年收获的橄榄的新鲜压榨的橄榄油——这通常是巴勒斯坦历法中的欢乐时刻，她说现在感觉苦乐参半。今年，被占领的约旦河西岸巴勒斯坦人的橄榄收成因以色列定居者的频繁袭击而受到破坏，他们试图扰乱一年中这个具有重要经济和文化意义的时期。
10 月 27 日，以色列萨赫宁举行的以色列大选首个出口民意调查结果公布后，以色列议会议员、保守派穆斯林拉姆党领袖曼苏尔·阿巴斯拥抱了一名支持者。Mahmoud Illean/美联社隐藏标题栏
以色列的巴勒斯坦公民是 1948 年以色列建国时留下的人的后裔（当时大多数战前人口在战争期间被强行驱逐或逃离），现在约占人口的 20%。
据中央选举委员会称，这次选举中，阿拉伯人领导的政党获得的选票比上次选举增加了 64%。他们所取得的成果激起了许多以色列政治右翼人士的愤怒甚至恐惧，他们认为这些成果对该国的犹太性格构成了威胁。
内塔尼亚胡和他的盟友以阿拉伯人的大量投票作为战斗口号。选举日当天，内塔尼亚胡发布了一段视频，称其为“紧急情况”。极右翼国家安全部长伊塔马尔·本·格维尔 (Itamar Ben Gvir) 在库夫尔·卡西姆 (Kufr Qasim) 入口处拍摄了自己的呼吁：“如果你希望这个国家继续是犹太人和犹太复国主义者……那就出去投票吧！”

title_en: The incoming class of U.S. senators is full of historic firsts
title_zh: 即将上任的美国参议员充满了历史性的第一
summary: From the first Native American woman elected to the U.S. Senate and the first Muslim who will join the upper chamber to the Senate's first Paralympian, voters elected historic candidates on Tuesday.
summary_zh: 从第一位当选美国参议院议员的美国原住民女性、第一位进入参议院的穆斯林到参议院第一位残奥会运动员
body_en: Josh Turek, Peggy Flanagan, and Dr. Abdul El-Sayed are among several Democratic Senators-elect who made history on Election Day 2026. Scott Olson/Getty Images; Dymanh Chhoun/Sahan Journal/CatchLight via Getty Images; Sylvia Jarrus for NPR hide caption
When the newest class of U.S. senators are sworn into office in January, it will include some of America's firsts .
These 10 candidates for governor made history in the 2026 election

The 2026 midterm election resulted in a significant shift in the landscape of Congress as Democrats won in a big way up and down the ballot. While not all the races have been called, Democrats have flipped more than 40 House seats and picked up 7 Senate seats, giving them control of both chambers of Congress.
Here are some of the new faces to expect in the Senate who made history on Election Day.
Josh Turek speaks during an election night event Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026, in Des Moines, Iowa. Ellen Schmidt/AP hide caption

Turek will be the first Paralympian to serve in the Senate. The Democrat is a two-time gold medalist in wheelchair basketball. Turek is paraplegic and uses a wheelchair due to spina bifida. He beat Republican Ashley Hinson in the general election.
Julia Letlow speaks to media during an election night watch party on May 16, 2026, in Baton Rouge, La. Matthew Hinton/AP hide caption

Letlow has now made history twice. She was the first Republican woman elected to the U.S. House from Louisiana in 2021. Letlow ran for the House in a special election to replace her late husband, Congressman Luke Letlow, who died of COVID-19 in 2020. Now, Louisiana voters have decided to send her to the Senate, where she will be the first Republican woman from the state to serve. She will succeed Republican Sen. Bill Cassidy, who Letlow beat in the primary election.
Dr. Abdul El-Sayed visits a polling precinct on the campus of the University of Michigan on November 3, 2026 in Ann Arbor, Mich. Salwan Georges/Getty Images hide caption

The incoming Democratic senator is the son of Egyptian immigrants and is the first Muslim person elected to the upper chamber. El-Sayed is an epidemiologist and the former health director for the city of Detroit. He beat Republican Mike Rogers for the hotly contested seat.
Peggy Flanagan walks with her husband as they arrive to vote at a polling location on Election Day in St. Louis Park, Minn. on November 3, 2026. Tim Evans/AFP via Getty Images hide caption

Minnesota's Democratic Lt. Governor is the first Native American woman elected to the Senate. Flanagan is a member of the White Earth Band of Ojibwe. She also made political history more than once. She was also the first woman of color elected to state office in Minnesota. Flanagan will replace outgoing Democratic Sen. Tina Smith.
Chris Pappas walks onstage to deliver his acceptance speech at a watch party at the Puritan Backroom on November 3, 2026 in Manchester, New Hampshire. Joseph Prezioso/Getty Images hide caption

Pappas is the first openly gay man elected to the Senate and is also the first gay man to represent the state of New Hampshire. He served four terms in the House and beat Republican John Sununu in the election.
Dr. Annie Andrews takes the stage at an election night event in Charleston, S.C. on November 3, 2026. Mic Smith/AP hide caption

In one of the biggest election night upsets, Andrews pulled out an underdog win in deep red South Carolina. Andrews is the first woman elected to the U.S. senate from the Palmetto State. She beat Darline Graham, who was appointed to replace her late brother Lindsey Graham.
Democratic candidates James Talarico and Adam Hamilton won their Senate races in Texas and Kansas, respectively. Ronaldo Schemidt/AFP via Getty Images; Charlie Riedel/AP hide caption
Both states are reliably Republican and both states are sending pastors to Washington. This midterm election voters broke with the status quo and elected Democrats to represent them in the Senate.
body_zh: 乔什·图雷克 (Josh Turek)、佩吉·弗拉纳根 (Peggy Flanagan) 和阿卜杜勒·埃尔-赛义德 (Abdul El-Sayed) 博士等几位当选民主党参议员在 2026 年选举日创造了历史。斯科特·奥尔森/盖蒂图片社； Dymanh Chhoun/Sahan Journal/CatchLight 来自 Getty Images； NPR 的西尔维娅·贾勒斯隐藏标题栏
当最新一批美国参议员在一月份宣誓就职时，其中将包括一些美国的第一。
这10位州长候选人在2026年选举中创造了历史
2026 年中期选举导致国会格局发生重大转变，民主党在选票上大幅获胜。虽然并非所有竞选都已结束，但民主党已经翻转了 40 多个众议院席位，并赢得了 7 个参议院席位，从而控制了国会两院。
以下是参议院中值得期待的一些新面孔，他们在选举日创造了历史。
乔什·图雷克 (Josh Turek) 于 2026 年 11 月 3 日星期二在爱荷华州得梅因举行的选举之夜活动中发表讲话。艾伦·施密特/美联社隐藏标题栏
图雷克将成为第一位在参议院任职的残奥会运动员。这位民主党人曾两次获得轮椅篮球金牌。由于脊柱裂，图雷克截瘫并需要使用轮椅。他在大选中击败了共和党人阿什利·辛森。
2026 年 5 月 16 日，路易斯安那州巴吞鲁日，朱莉娅·莱特洛 (Julia Letlow) 在选举守夜派对上向媒体发表讲话。马修·辛顿 (Matthew Hinton)/美联社 隐藏标题栏
莱特洛现已两次创造历史。她是 2021 年路易斯安那州第一位当选美国众议院议员的共和党女性。莱特洛在一次特别选举中竞选众议院议员，以取代她已故的丈夫、国会议员卢克·莱特洛（后者于 2020 年因 COVID-19 去世）。现在，路易斯安那州选民决定将她送往参议院，她将成为该州第一位任职的共和党女性。她将接替莱特洛在初选中击败的共和党参议员比尔·卡西迪。
2026 年 11 月 3 日，阿卜杜勒·赛义德博士参观了位于密歇根州安阿伯市的密歇根大学校园内的投票区。Salwan Georges/Getty Images 隐藏标题栏
即将上任的民主党参议员是埃及移民的儿子，也是第一位当选参议院议员的穆斯林人士。埃尔-赛义德是一位流行病学家，也是底特律市前卫生总监。他击败了共和党人迈克·罗杰斯，赢得了竞争激烈的席位。
2026 年 11 月 3 日，佩吉·弗拉纳根 (Peggy Flanagan) 与丈夫一起前往明尼苏达州圣路易斯公园的选举日投票站投票。蒂姆·埃文斯 (Tim Evans)/法新社 (盖蒂图片社) 隐藏标题栏
明尼苏达州的民主党副州长是第一位当选参议员的美国原住民女性。弗拉纳根是奥及布威白土乐队的成员。她还不止一次创造了政治历史。她也是明尼苏达州第一位当选州政府官员的有色人种女性。弗拉纳根将接替即将卸任的民主党参议员蒂娜·史密斯。
2026 年 11 月 3 日，新罕布什尔州曼彻斯特，克里斯·帕帕斯 (Chris Pappas) 在清教徒后台 (Puritan Backroom) 举行的观看派对上走上舞台发表获奖感言。约瑟夫·普雷齐奥索/盖蒂图片社隐藏标题栏
帕帕斯是第一位当选参议员的公开同性恋者，也是第一位代表新罕布什尔州的同性恋者。他在众议院连任四届，并在选举中击败了共和党人约翰·苏努努。
安妮·安德鲁斯博士于 2026 年 11 月 3 日在南卡罗来纳州查尔斯顿举行的选举之夜活动上登台。Mic Smith/美联社隐藏标题栏
在选举之夜最大的冷门之一中，安德鲁斯在深红色的南卡罗来纳州取得了一场失败的胜利。安德鲁斯是第一位从帕尔梅托州当选为美国参议员的女性。她击败了达林·格雷厄姆，后者被任命接替她已故的兄弟林赛·格雷厄姆。
民主党候选人詹姆斯·塔拉里科和亚当·汉密尔顿分别赢得了德克萨斯州和堪萨斯州的参议员竞选。罗纳尔多·施密特/法新社，盖蒂图片社；查理·里德尔/美联社隐藏标题栏
这两个州都是可靠的共和党州，并且都派牧师到华盛顿。这次中期选举选民打破现状，选举民主党人在参议院代表他们。

title_en: Jay Rockefeller, former West Virginia governor and US senator, dies at 89
title_zh: 前西弗吉尼亚州州长、美国参议员杰伊·洛克菲勒去世，享年 89 岁
summary: Jay Rockefeller, the last member of his family’s political dynasty who served as West Virginia’s governor and later a longtime U.S. senator, has died
summary_zh: 杰伊·洛克菲勒 (Jay Rockefeller) 去世，他是其家族政治王朝的最后一位成员，曾担任西弗吉尼亚州州长，后来长期担任美国参议员。
body_en: Election 2026 live results: Nithya Raman promises smooth transition of power to LA mayor
Nithya Raman promises smooth transition of power
Georgia Governor-elect Keisha Lance Bottoms on her historic win and working with Trump
Jay Rockefeller, the last member of his family’s political dynasty who served as West Virginia’s governor and later a longtime U.S. senator, has died

CHARLESTON, W.Va. -- Jay Rockefeller, the last member of his family’s political dynasty — and the only Democrat — who served as West Virginia’s governor and later a longtime U.S. senator, has died. He was 89.

Rockefeller died Thursday night at his home in Washington, said Mary Stewart, vice president for external affairs at WETA, the public broadcasting station where Rockefeller’s wife, Sharon, serves as president and CEO.

Rockefeller came from one of the nation’s richest families to spend a half century in public service in one of the poorest states. He arrived in 1964 as a worker in an anti-poverty program, was elected governor a dozen years later and served two terms, then spent 30 years as a U.S. senator.
“I could not imagine a more rewarding career,” Rockefeller said upon his retirement in 2015.

He was born John D. Rockefeller IV in New York City. His great-grandfather, Standard Oil Co. founder John Rockefeller, died a month before Rockefeller’s birth. His father, John D. Rockefeller III, was a well-known philanthropist. Uncles Winthrop (Arkansas) and Nelson (New York) were Republican governors. Another uncle, David Rockefeller, ran Chase Manhattan Bank.
Jay Rockefeller went in a different direction.

A few years out of college at age 27, Rockefeller moved to the West Virginia mining community of Emmons to participate in the Volunteers in Service to America program, a time that Rockefeller said proved transformative.

“It explains every policy I pursued and every vote I have cast. It was where my beliefs were bolted down, and where my passions met my principles,” he said in an emotional farewell speech from the Senate floor on Dec. 4, 2014.

While he intended for his stay in the state to be brief, Rockefeller broke from his family’s Republican tradition and was elected to the state House of Delegates as a Democrat in 1966. By combining money with hard work in a traditionally Democratic state, Rockefeller overcame suspicions of political opportunism and rose from state legislator to secretary of state to governor.

A turning point came after Rockefeller’s only political defeat in the 1972 governor’s race to Republican Arch A. Moore Jr., whose daughter, Republican Shelley Moore Capito, was elected in 2014 to Rockefeller’s Senate seat upon his retirement. Capito on Friday called Rockefeller “a true gentleman" who treated her with respect, kindness and encouragement.
“Over the years, we developed a wonderful friendship that transcended politics, and I will always be grateful for that,” she said in a statement.

After the defeat, Rockefeller remained in West Virginia, a decision he called the most important of his career. He became the first without a theological degree to become president of West Virginia Wesleyan College in 1973. His popularity there — and a change in his stance to embrace strip mining — translated to a landslide win over Republican Cecil Underwood in the 1976 governor’s race.

As governor, Rockefeller emphasized development of the state’s infrastructure, such as roads, sewers and bridges. Those issues, he said, are “not very sexy things, I grant you but very, very necessary in West Virginia.”

杰伊·洛克菲勒 (Jay Rockefeller) 去世，他是其家族政治王朝的最后一位成员，曾担任西弗吉尼亚州州长，后来长期担任美国参议员。
西弗吉尼亚州查尔斯顿——杰伊·洛克菲勒去世，他是其家族政治王朝的最后一位成员，也是唯一的民主党人，曾担任西弗吉尼亚州州长，后来担任长期美国参议员。他89岁了。
WETA 公共广播电台负责对外事务的副总裁玛丽·斯图尔特 (Mary Stewart) 说，洛克菲勒周四晚上在华盛顿的家中去世。
洛克菲勒来自美国最富有的家庭之一，在最贫穷的州之一从事公共服务工作了半个世纪。 1964 年，他作为反贫困计划的一名工作人员来到美国，十几年后当选为州长并连任两届，然后担任了 30 年的美国参议员。
“我无法想象还有比这更有价值的职业了，”洛克菲勒在 2015 年退休时说道。
他出生于纽约市，原名约翰·D·洛克菲勒四世。他的曾祖父、标准石油公司创始人约翰·洛克菲勒在洛克菲勒出生前一个月去世。他的父亲约翰·D·洛克菲勒三世是一位著名的慈善家。温思罗普叔叔（阿肯色州）和纳尔逊叔叔（纽约州）是共和党州长。另一位叔叔大卫·洛克菲勒经营着大通曼哈顿银行。
杰·洛克菲勒却走向了不同的方向。
27 岁的洛克菲勒大学毕业几年后，搬到了西弗吉尼亚州埃蒙斯采矿社区，参加了“为美国服务志愿者”计划，洛克菲勒称这段时期具有变革性。
2014 年 12 月 4 日，他在参议院发表感人的告别演说时表示，“它解释了我奉行的每一项政策和我投下的每一张选票。在这里，我的信仰得到了坚定，我的热情与我的原则相遇了。”
虽然洛克菲勒本打算在该州停留很短的时间，但他打破了家族的共和党传统，并于 1966 年以民主党人身份当选为州众议院议员。通过在传统的民主党州将金钱与辛勤工作结合起来，洛克菲勒克服了对政治机会主义的怀疑，从州议员晋升为国务卿，再到州长。

1972 年，洛克菲勒在与共和党小阿奇·A·摩尔 (Arch A. Moore Jr.) 的州长竞选中遭遇唯一一次政治失败后，出现了转折点。摩尔·小摩尔 (Arch A. Moore Jr.) 的女儿、共和党人雪莱·摩尔·卡皮托 (Shelley Moore Capito) 于 2014 年在洛克菲勒退休后当选为洛克菲勒参议院席位。卡皮托周五称洛克菲勒是“一位真正的绅士”，他对她表示尊重、友善和鼓励。
她在一份声明中说：“多年来，我们建立了超越政治的美好友谊，我将永远对此表示感激。”
失败后，洛克菲勒留在西弗吉尼亚州，他称这是他职业生涯中最重要的决定。 1973 年，他成为第一个没有神学学位的西弗吉尼亚卫斯理学院院长。他在那里的受欢迎程度以及他拥抱露天采矿的立场的转变，最终在 1976 年州长竞选中以压倒性优势击败了共和党人塞西尔·安德伍德。
作为州长，洛克菲勒强调发展该州的基础设施，如道路、下水道和桥梁。他说，这些问题“不是很性感的事情，我承认，但在西弗吉尼亚州非常非常必要。”

title_en: The size of Democrats’ wave surprised even their top House super PAC
title_zh: 民主党浪潮的规模甚至令他们的众议院超级政治行动委员会感到惊讶
summary: House Majority PAC President Mike Smith said Democrats’ gains are “on the very high end” of the group’s expectations.
summary_zh: 众议院多数党政治行动委员会主席迈克·史密斯表示，民主党的进展“处于该组织预期的非常高的水平”。
body_en: Even the head of House Democrats’ top super PAC didn’t fully anticipate the size of their massive midterm wave.

Heading into Election Day, House Majority PAC president Mike Smith told POLITICO Tuesday’s results, which have netted them a whopping 252 House seats with more yet to be called, was “on the very high end” of the group’s expectations.

The group spent at least $283 million on ads this cycle, per ad-tracking firm AdImpact, making them the largest Democratic spender in House races this cycle and a significant force behind the party’s big night.
As Democrats turn their attention to 2028, Smith remains optimistic the party can hold on to its majority.
His confidence stems in part from a projection that Democrats will respond to the affordability concerns that were the core of the party’s promise to voters.
If Democrats don’t make efforts to address the rising cost of living, “then it's a totally different story,” Smith said.
Q: How were you feeling in the final days before Tuesday?

Obviously this would have been on the very high end of what we expected. Over the last three months, overall our polling has been pretty consistent. Our whole thought was, with the right environment, if we have the right message and the right types of candidates in, not just the 50-50 districts, but like deeper in the map, that we could put those seats in play and we could potentially win.

Going into Election Day, our whole feeling was there's a clear path to like 235-plus [seats]. We were playing in districts that, if you were to rank them from like one to 435, some of those districts were like 250, 255, right? And I would throw IN-05, CO-03, KY-06, SC-01, some of the Florida races. SC-01 wasn't ever going to be seat 225. That was always in the 240s and maybe even 250s. But we took a chance because we saw what the national environment looked like. We saw what the data was coming back in within these individual races. So I think we were optimistic. But to be totally honest, in our heads, you have to play in seat 255 to get to seat 240. You have to spread out the map. You have to force Republicans on their heels, and then you start piecing together how you get to the 240-245 range. Once the numbers started coming back, that was the best case scenario for us. Everything came together.

You guys cut reservations in some reach districts, only to go back up in the final few days. On the outside, it appeared like cutting spending in those reach districts was a bad sign. What went into those last-minute spending decisions?

A lot of the places we made reservations back in April, and then continued to add on to that over the course of the summer. Partners and allies in a bunch of different places took over our reservations. We tried to be smart by locking in the lowest possible rates in very expensive markets, [so that] even if HMP wasn't the entity spending, we still had partners and allies that were taking over their reservations. In doing all that we saved about $130 million that we could reinvest.

The challenge with some of the races was by a week out, our money was spent. And in some of those districts, there weren't any partners willing to step up and do it. Florida is a good example of that.

That’s where we just had to make a decision that there weren't the resources there, and we had to leave the reservations on the table. Around that time, Mayor Bloomberg was like , "We can't let these races get away from us. We need to do everything we can," and that's where we went back into some of those places.
Did you feel the need to adjust your messaging at all once MAGA Inc. and Elon Musk’s PAC joined CLF on the airwaves?

The short answer is no. The messaging was fairly consistent. Early on, our whole feeling was we need to reframe how voters perceive Democrats. When voters think about what Democrats are fighting for, the first thing we want them to think about is cost of living, the economy. At the same time, bringing to light Republican policies that are increasing the cost of living, or focus on things that are anything but that.

Over several months, we did a bunch of battleground research looking at ‘how does corruption tie into that,’ which culminated in what we would describe as the cost of Republican corruption, and how that is impacting your day to day and your cost of living. That's what we went into Election Day with.

Overall, we ran, I don't know, 1300 different types of ads, whether TV, digital, direct mail, or whatnot. 76% of those ads talked about the economy. 60% of those ads focused on corruption, because in so many of them, those two things were interlinked in voters' minds.

Republicans continued to focus on the same thing. It was trying to paint Democrats as out of touch or extremists. And again, the theory of the case from the beginning was us focusing on economic concerns, especially when we figured out we could tie that corruption lens into it. That's going to be more important to voters than folks talking about socialism or anything else.
Democrats were able to prevent Republicans from capitalizing on their redistricting gains. Are you worried about those gains bearing fruit in a less favorable environment, maybe as soon as 2028?

In a different environment, these races are going to come together in a much different way. So I do think it's something that we need to be hyper-focused on. That said, I don't think redistricting is going to go away.
body_zh: 就连众议院民主党最高政治行动委员会的负责人也没有完全预料到中期选举浪潮的规模。
临近选举日，众议院多数派政治行动委员会主席迈克·史密斯 (Mike Smith) 告诉《政治》杂志，周二的选举结果让他们获得了多达 252 个众议院席位，更多席位尚未公布，这“处于该集团预期的最高水平”。
根据广告跟踪公司 AdImpact 的数据，该集团在本周期的广告上花费了至少 2.83 亿美元，使他们成为本周期众议院竞选中民主党支出最多的人，也是该党盛大夜晚背后的重要力量。
随着民主党将注意力转向 2028 年，史密斯仍然乐观地认为该党能够保住多数席位。
他的信心部分源于对民主党将回应负担能力担忧的预测，这是该党对选民承诺的核心。
史密斯说，如果民主党不努力解决生活成本上升的问题，“那么情况就完全不同了”。
问：周二之前的最后几天你感觉如何？
显然，这超出了我们的预期。在过去的三个月里，我们的民意调查总体上非常一致。我们的整体想法是，在合适的环境下，如果我们有正确的信息和正确类型的候选人，不仅仅是在 50-50 选区，而且在地图的更深处，我们就可以让这些席位发挥作用，我们就有可能获胜。

进入选举日，我们的整体感觉是有一条明确的道路可以赢得 235 个以上的[席位]。我们比赛的地区，如果你把它们从 1 到 435 进行排名，其中一些地区就像 250、255，对吗？我会参加 IN-05、CO-03、KY-06、SC-01 以及佛罗里达州的一些比赛。 SC-01 永远不会是 225 号座位。那总是在 240 到 250 之间。但我们抓住了机会，因为我们看到了国家环境的样子。我们看到了这些个人比赛中返回的数据。所以我认为我们很乐观。但说实话，在我们看来，你必须在 255 号座位上玩才能到达 240 号座位。你必须展开地图。你必须迫使共和党人紧随其后，然后你开始拼凑如何达到 240-245 的范围。一旦数字开始回升，这对我们来说就是最好的情况。一切都在一起了。
你们削减了一些地区的预订，但在最后几天又恢复了预订。从表面上看，削减这些地区的支出似乎是一个坏兆头。最后一刻的支出决定是出于什么考虑？
我们在四月份就预订了很多地方，然后在整个夏天继续增加预订。许多不同地方的合作伙伴和盟友接管了我们的预订。我们试图通过在非常昂贵的市场中锁定尽可能低的利率来变得聪明，[这样]即使 HMP 不是实体支出，我们仍然有合作伙伴和盟友接管他们的预订。通过这一切，我们节省了大约 1.3 亿美元，可以进行再投资。
有些比赛的挑战是一周后，我们的钱就花完了。在其中一些地区，没有任何合作伙伴愿意站出来这样做。佛罗里达州就是一个很好的例子。
在那里，我们必须做出决定，因为那里没有资源，所以我们必须保留保留意见。大约在那个时候，布隆伯格市长说，“我们不能让这些种族远离我们。我们需要尽我们所能，”这就是我们回到其中一些地方的地方。
当 MAGA Inc. 和埃隆·马斯克的 PAC 加入 CLF 后，您是否觉得有必要在广播中调整您的信息？
简短的回答是否定的。消息传递相当一致。早些时候，我们的整体感觉是我们需要重新构建选民对民主党的看法。当选民思考民主党为何而战时，我们希望他们首先考虑的是生活成本和经济。与此同时，揭露共和党正在增加生活成本的政策，或者关注的不是生活成本。
在几个月的时间里，我们做了一系列战场研究，着眼于“腐败与腐败有何联系”，最终得出了我们所说的共和党腐败成本，以及它如何影响你的日常生活和生活成本。这就是我们进入选举日的原因。
总的来说，我不知道，我们投放了 1300 个不同类型的广告，无论是电视广告、数字广告、直邮广告还是其他广告。其中 76% 的广告谈到了经济。其中 60% 的广告聚焦于腐败，因为在很多广告中，这两件事在选民的心目中是相互关联的。
共和党人继续关注同一件事。它试图将民主党描绘成脱离现实或极端分子。再说一次，这个案例的理论从一开始就是我们关注经济问题，特别是当我们发现我们可以将腐败镜头与它联系起来时。对于选民来说，这比人们谈论社会主义或其他任何事情更重要。
民主党能够阻止共和党利用其重新划分选区的成果。您是否担心这些成果会在不太有利的环境下（也许最早到 2028 年）结出硕果？
在不同的环境中，这些种族将以截然不同的方式聚集在一起。所以我确实认为这是我们需要高度关注的事情。也就是说，我认为选区重新划分不会消失。

President Trump has replaced White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller, the hard-line architect of his immigration agenda, following that crushing midterm defeat. Immigration, once a political strength for Mr. Trump, has become a liability after two years of mass detentions, deportations, and armed agents in American cities.

Mr. Trump pledged to work with the incoming Democratic Congress, but Miller's appointment signals a doubling down on his agenda. Miller has called Democrats a -- quote -- "domestic extremist organization."
Liz Landers reports on the appointment and the GOP's post-election reckoning.
Today, at the White House, President Trump defiant in his choice.
Stephen's been with me from beginning. He gets it, very good politically, and he's a very good manager. He will do a great job, great manager.
The fallout from the midterm elections reaching his inner circle.
I wanted to make a change. I think Susie's done a very good job, great job, but I just wanted to make it. Stephen's been great. And we got to make -- we have got to make moves.

Trump announced this afternoon that Susie Wiles, his chief of staff, is stepping down. She was the first woman to hold the role and was Trump's longest tenured chief of staff. Wiles will be replaced by Stephen Miller, the current deputy chief of staff.

Miller is one of Washington's most polarizing power brokers. He's a chief architect of the administration's immigration crackdown, but his portfolio has expanded to include national security issues. Meanwhile, for Trump, a president who made loyalty to him a defining test of his party, criticism now comes from within it.
And I think the Republican voters are more upset about what's going on in Iran than the Democrat voters.
Oversight Chairman James Comer acknowledged the unpopular war that the Trump administration launched and questioned the defense secretary's role.
I can tell you with a high level of confidence that there's a lot of questions about Hegseth. We have no idea what the strategy is moving forward in Iran.
You see, they attack me, they attack us because we are effective.
The secretary of defense defending himself in a video posted on social media as an outgoing Republican member of Congress could force a vote to impeach the secretary as early as next week.
It's all about the politics of personal destruction. Didn't work against President Trump, and it won't work with me.
body_zh: 在中期惨败后，特朗普用他的移民议程的强硬派设计师斯蒂芬·米勒取代了白宫办公厅主任苏西·怀尔斯。移民曾经是特朗普的政治优势，但在美国城市两年的大规模拘留、驱逐和武装特工之后，移民变成了一种负担。米勒的任命标志着特朗普议程上的加倍努力。莉兹·兰德斯报道。

在中期选举惨败后，特朗普总统用他的移民议程的强硬派设计师斯蒂芬·米勒取代了白宫办公厅主任苏西·怀尔斯。移民曾经是特朗普的政治优势，但在美国城市经历了两年的大规模拘留、驱逐和武装特工之后，移民已成为一种负担。
特朗普承诺与即将上任的民主党国会合作，但米勒的任命标志着他的议程加倍努力。米勒称民主党为“国内极端主义组织”。
利兹·兰德斯报道了这一任命和共和党的选举后清算。
今天，在白宫，特朗普总统对他的选择表示蔑视。
斯蒂芬从一开始就和我在一起。他明白这一点，政治上非常出色，而且他是一位非常优秀的经理。他会做得很好，伟大的经理。
中期选举的影响波及到了他的核心圈子。
我想做出改变。我认为苏西做得非常好，非常棒，但我只是想成功。斯蒂芬很棒。我们必须采取行动。
特朗普今天下午宣布，他的幕僚长苏西·威尔斯将辞职。她是第一位担任该职位的女性，也是特朗普任期最长的幕僚长。怀尔斯将由现任副参谋长斯蒂芬·米勒接替。
米勒是华盛顿最两极分化的权力掮客之一。他是政府打击移民的总设计师，但他的职责范围已扩大到包括国家安全问题。与此同时，对于特朗普这个将对他的忠诚度视为对其政党的决定性考验的总统来说，现在的批评来自于党内。
我认为共和党选民比民主党选民对伊朗正在发生的事情更感到不安。
监督委员会主席詹姆斯·科默承认特朗普政府发动了这场不受欢迎的战争，并对国防部长的角色提出了质疑。
我可以非常有信心地告诉你，关于赫格斯有很多问题。我们不知道伊朗正在推进什么战略。

Stevie Bonifield is a news writer covering all things consumer tech. Stevie started out at Laptop Mag writing news and reviews on hardware, gaming, and AI.

OpenAI is now valued at $1.25 trillion in a new round of funding that has raised another $11 billion, according to Bloomberg . That would make it one of the world’s most valuable companies, not long after raising $122 billion from investors in March at a valuation of $852 billion.

Echoing FT and Wall Street Journal reports from last week, Bloomberg says OpenAI is still pursuing additional investments that could increase the amount to $20 billion, and that it had initially hoped to raise as much as $30 billion at a higher valuation of $1.4 trillion. That was before tech stocks dropped, and the results of the midterms showed how much public opinion has turned against AI companies and data center projects .

OpenAI’s rival Anthropic filed its S-1 to go public last week. Earlier this year, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said it’s holding off on its own IPO until it can make more confident claims about its models’ safety. He didn’t give a specific timeline for the IPO, but said at the time, “I think it’s also kind of bad for the world if OpenAI waits too long to go public.”
